why.headline: Why is the sky blue?
why.summary: Sunlight is all colours mixed. Air molecules bounce the blue part around more than the rest, so blue hits your eyes from every direction.

why.try: Watch a far hill and a close fence on the same ride.
why.tryLine: Watch a far hill and a close fence on the same ride.

why.headline: Why does the Moon change shape?
why.summary: The Moon is always a ball. We only see the half the Sun lights. As it orbits us, that lit half turns toward or away from Earth.
why.try: Draw the Moon tonight. Draw it again in 3 days.
why.tryLine: Draw the Moon tonight. Draw it again in 3 days.

why.headline: Why do stars twinkle?
why.summary: Starlight squeezes through wobbly air, like looking through a swimming pool. Planets look steadier because they are tiny disks, not pinpoints.
why.try: Find a bright 'star' that does not twinkle. It might be a planet.
why.tryLine: Find a bright 'star' that does not twinkle. It might be a planet.

why.headline: Why is space black if the Sun is there?
why.summary: Space has almost no air to bounce light into your eyes. The Sun lights what it hits. Empty sky stays dark.
why.try: Shine a torch in a dark room. The beam is invisible until it hits dust.
why.tryLine: Shine a torch in a dark room. The beam is invisible until it hits dust.

why.headline: Why do astronauts float?
why.summary: They are falling around Earth, and the station falls at the same speed. Same fall = float. Not 'no gravity' — plenty of gravity.
why.try: Jump in a lift that just started down. That tiny light feeling is a hint.
why.tryLine: Jump in a lift that just started down. That tiny light feeling is a hint.

why.headline: Why do we have seasons?
why.summary: Earth is tilted. For part of the year your half leans toward the Sun (longer, stronger days). Then it leans away. Distance to the Sun is not the main reason.
why.try: Check sunset time this week vs a month ago.
why.tryLine: Check sunset time this week vs a month ago.

why.headline: Why do we get a leap day?
why.summary: Earth's trip around the Sun is about 365 and a quarter days. Those quarters add up. Every four years we park the extra day in February.
why.try: Ask what year you were born. Was it a leap year?
why.tryLine: Ask what year you were born. Was it a leap year?

why.headline: Why does the wind blow?
why.summary: Sun heats land and air unevenly. Warm air rises. Cooler air rushes in to fill the gap. That rush is wind.
why.try: Stand at a door between a warm room and a cold one. Feel the sneak draft.
why.tryLine: Stand at a door between a warm room and a cold one. Feel the sneak draft.

why.headline: Why don't clouds fall?
why.summary: Cloud drops are tiny and light. Air holds them up like dust in a sunbeam. When drops join and get heavy, they fall as rain.
why.try: Watch a kettle steam. Same idea, smaller cloud.
why.tryLine: Watch a kettle steam. Same idea, smaller cloud.

why.headline: Why does rain have a smell?
why.summary: Dry ground holds oily plant bits and soil bacteria gases. First drops splash them into the air. That earthy sniff has a name: petrichor.
why.try: Smell the pavement at the start of the next shower.
why.tryLine: Smell the pavement at the start of the next shower.

why.headline: Why is snow so quiet?
why.summary: Fresh snow is full of air pockets. Sound sinks in instead of bouncing. The world goes muffled, like a blanket on a drum.
why.try: Listen outside after new snow, then after it melts.
why.tryLine: Listen outside after new snow, then after it melts.

why.headline: Why does ice float?
why.summary: Most solids sink in their own liquid. Water is weird: frozen water takes more space, so ice is lighter than liquid water. Lakes freeze from the top, and fish keep a home underneath.
why.try: Drop an ice cube in a glass. It sits up top.
why.tryLine: Drop an ice cube in a glass. It sits up top.

why.headline: Why does salt melt ice on roads?
why.summary: Salt makes it harder for water to stay frozen. The mix needs a colder temperature to be ice, so many winter roads turn slushy.
why.try: Sprinkle a pinch of salt on an ice cube and watch.
why.tryLine: Sprinkle a pinch of salt on an ice cube and watch.

why.headline: Why do we yawn?
why.summary: Scientists still argue. A strong idea: yawning cools the brain a bit and wakes you up. Seeing someone yawn is contagious because brains copy each other.
why.try: Try not to yawn while reading this. Good luck.
why.tryLine: Try not to yawn while reading this. Good luck.

why.headline: Why do we get hiccups?
why.summary: Your diaphragm — the breathing muscle — spasms. The 'hic' is the voice-box flap snapping shut. Usually it stops on its own.
why.try: Sip water slowly next time. No need for wild tricks.
why.tryLine: Sip water slowly next time. No need for wild tricks.

why.headline: Why do we get goosebumps?
why.summary: Tiny muscles lift each hair. In furry animals that makes a warmer, scarier coat. Humans kept the reflex. Cold or a spooky film can still fire it.
why.try: Notice them on your arm in a cold room.
why.tryLine: Notice them on your arm in a cold room.

why.headline: Why do fingers wrinkle in the bath?
why.summary: Nerves tell the skin to wrinkle on purpose. The ridges grip wet things better, like tyre treads. It is not just skin soaking up water.
why.try: Compare a dry fingertip and a bath fingertip on a wet glass.
why.tryLine: Compare a dry fingertip and a bath fingertip on a wet glass.

why.headline: Why does a stomach rumble?
why.summary: Your gut squeezes even when it is empty. Air and juices slosh. With no food to muffle the sound, the room hears it.
why.try: It is not always hunger. Sometimes it is just plumbing.
why.tryLine: It is not always hunger. Sometimes it is just plumbing.

why.headline: Why do echoes happen?
why.summary: Sound is a bounce. A hard cliff or sports hall sends the wave back. If the trip is long enough, you hear yourself late.
why.try: Clap once in a stairwell. Then clap in a sofa room.
why.tryLine: Clap once in a stairwell. Then clap in a sofa room.

why.headline: Why do mirrors flip left and right?
why.summary: They flip front to back, not left to right. Your 'right hand' still points the same way. It looks swapped because you imagine turning around to face yourself.
why.try: Write a word on paper and hold it to a mirror.
why.tryLine: Write a word on paper and hold it to a mirror.

why.headline: Why does helium make your voice funny?
why.summary: Sound speed is faster in helium than in air. Your voice box shapes the same mouth moves, but the pitch jumps up. It wears off as you breathe air again.
why.try: Don't try this without a grown-up and proper party helium.
why.tryLine: Don't try this without a grown-up and proper party helium.

why.headline: Why does popcorn pop?
why.summary: A hard shell traps water. Heat turns that water to steam. Pressure builds until the kernel explodes into a fluffy starch cloud.
why.try: Listen: each pop is a tiny steam bomb.
why.tryLine: Listen: each pop is a tiny steam bomb.

why.headline: Why does bread rise?
why.summary: Yeast eats sugar and burps carbon dioxide. Those gas bubbles puff the dough. Heat locks the bubbles in place.
why.try: Watch dough on a radiator for an hour.
why.tryLine: Watch dough on a radiator for an hour.

why.headline: Why do cut apples go brown?
why.summary: A cut lets air hit an enzyme in the fruit. It rusts the surface, basically. Lemon juice slows it.
why.try: Cut two slices. Lemon on one. Compare in 10 minutes.
why.tryLine: Cut two slices. Lemon on one. Compare in 10 minutes.

why.headline: Why are tears salty?
why.summary: Your body is a salty ocean in disguise. Tears wash the eye with a mix like diluted seawater. Sweat is salty for the same family of reasons.
why.try: Taste is optional. Trust the science.
why.tryLine: Taste is optional. Trust the science.

why.headline: Why is blood red?
why.summary: Haemoglobin carries oxygen using iron. That iron-oxygen combo looks red. Some animals use copper instead and their blood is blue-green.
why.try: Octopus blood is blue. You already knew they have three hearts.
why.tryLine: Octopus blood is blue. You already knew they have three hearts.

why.headline: Why is yawning catching?
why.summary: Brains copy. Seeing a yawn can trigger yours. It may help a group stay alert together. Dogs can catch yawns from people too.
why.try: Yawn at a dog. Science says maybe.
why.tryLine: Yawn at a dog. Science says maybe.

why.headline: Why do dogs turn before they lie down?
why.summary: Wild ancestors flattened grass and checked for lumps or snakes. Your sofa dog still runs the old program. A few spins, then flop.
why.try: Count the spins tonight.
why.tryLine: Count the spins tonight.

why.headline: Why do cats purr?
why.summary: Purrs show up when cats are happy, hurt, or healing. The vibration may help bones and muscles. It is not only a 'I love you' button.
why.try: Feel a purr with your hand, not just your ears.
why.tryLine: Feel a purr with your hand, not just your ears.

why.headline: Why can chameleons change colour?
why.summary: Special skin cells shuffle pigments and crystals. They use it for mood, heat, and hiding. It is not just copy-the-sofa magic.
why.try: Watch a colour-change video in slow motion.
why.tryLine: Watch a colour-change video in slow motion.

why.headline: Why are flamingos pink?
why.summary: They eat shrimp and algae packed with pink dyes. Feather colour is lunch, not a factory setting. Pale food, pale bird.
why.try: If you only ate blueberries… not quite, but same idea.
why.tryLine: If you only ate blueberries… not quite, but same idea.

why.headline: Why don't woodpeckers get headaches?
why.summary: A thick skull, tiny brain play, and a tongue that wraps like a seatbelt. The beak hits, the shock spreads. Helmets wish they were this good.
why.try: Never copy this on a tree with your head.
why.tryLine: Never copy this on a tree with your head.

why.headline: Do fish sleep?
why.summary: They rest. Many slow down, some lie on the sand, a few parrotfish blow a mucus sleeping bag. No eyelids, so they look like they are staring.
why.try: Aquarium tip: night lights off, they calm down.
why.tryLine: Aquarium tip: night lights off, they calm down.

why.headline: Why do sharks sink if they stop swimming?
why.summary: Most fish have a balloon of gas. Sharks mostly don't. They stay up by swimming and using oily livers. Rest for them is still moving.
why.try: Not all sharks. Some can pump water while still.
why.tryLine: Not all sharks. Some can pump water while still.

why.headline: Why do volcanoes erupt?
why.summary: Melted rock is less dense than the rock around it, so it rises. Gas in the melt wants out. When the lid cracks, up it comes.
why.try: Fizzy drink + shake = baby version. Do it outside.
why.tryLine: Fizzy drink + shake = baby version. Do it outside.

why.headline: Why do earthquakes happen?
why.summary: Earth's crust is cracked into plates that creep. They stick, then slip. That slip shakes the ground.
why.try: If you ever feel one: drop, cover, hold on.
why.tryLine: If you ever feel one: drop, cover, hold on.

why.headline: Why do fossils exist?
why.summary: A dead thing gets buried fast, and minerals sneak into the shape. Bone turns to stone, more or less. Most living things never get that lucky.
why.try: Look for ripple marks in old stone walls.
why.tryLine: Look for ripple marks in old stone walls.

why.headline: Why did the non-bird dinosaurs vanish?
why.summary: A huge space rock hit Earth about 66 million years ago. Dust, dark, cold, then a ruined food chain. Birds are the dinosaurs that made it.
why.try: Next chicken dinner… that's a dinosaur cousin.
why.tryLine: Next chicken dinner… that's a dinosaur cousin.

why.headline: Why does a compass point north?
why.summary: Earth is a giant weak magnet. A compass needle lines up with that field. 'North' on the compass is magnetic north, a bit off true north.
why.try: Put a compass near a speaker. It will freak out.
why.tryLine: Put a compass near a speaker. It will freak out.

why.headline: Why do magnets stick to the fridge?
why.summary: Fridge doors have steel. Magnets yank on the tiny magnetic bits in that steel. They ignore wood, glass, and most plastic.
why.try: Test a coin, a spoon, and a pencil.
why.tryLine: Test a coin, a spoon, and a pencil.

why.headline: Why does a balloon stick to your hair?
why.summary: Rubbing moves electrons. The balloon and hair get opposite charges, so they pull together. Then your hair stands up because each hair shoves the next.
why.try: Try it on a dry day. Humidity ruins the trick.
why.tryLine: Try it on a dry day. Humidity ruins the trick.

why.headline: Why do batteries die?
why.summary: A battery is a controlled chemical race. When the chemicals are used up, the race stops. Cold slows the race. Heat can wreck it.
why.try: A 'dead' torch battery can still run a small clock. Different jobs, different leftover power.
why.tryLine: A 'dead' torch battery can still run a small clock. Different jobs, different leftover power.

why.headline: Why does a phone get hot?
why.summary: Work becomes heat. Games, charging, and bright screens make chips busy. The case is a tiny oven with nowhere for the heat to go.
why.try: Close extra apps and dim the screen. Instant cooler.
why.tryLine: Close extra apps and dim the screen. Instant cooler.

why.headline: Why can you see through glass?
why.summary: Glass has no tidy slots for visible light to get eaten. Photons cruise through. Metals have loose electrons that bounce light back, so they look shiny and solid.
why.try: Hold glass and foil to a lamp.
why.tryLine: Hold glass and foil to a lamp.

why.headline: Why do diamonds sparkle?
why.summary: The cut is a trap for light. Rays bounce around inside, then shoot out in flashes. A badly cut stone looks like a wet ice cube.
why.try: Sparkle is geometry plus light, not just 'being expensive'.
why.tryLine: Sparkle is geometry plus light, not just 'being expensive'.

why.headline: Why doesn't honey go off?
why.summary: Honey is dry, acidic, and packed with sugar that steals water from germs. Sealed well, it can last centuries. Tombs have proved it.
why.try: If it crystals, warm the jar gently. Still good.
why.tryLine: If it crystals, warm the jar gently. Still good.

why.headline: Why do onions make you cry?
why.summary: Cut cells spray a gas that turns into a mild acid in your eyes. Tears are the wash cycle. A sharp knife and cold onion help.
why.try: Don't rub your eyes. That spreads it.
why.tryLine: Don't rub your eyes. That spreads it.

why.headline: Why does mint feel cold?
why.summary: Menthol tricks cold sensors on your tongue. Nothing actually got colder. Your brain just got a fake weather report.
why.try: Mint gum on a winter day feels extra icy.
why.tryLine: Mint gum on a winter day feels extra icy.

why.headline: Why does chilli feel hot?
why.summary: Capsaicin flips pain-heat sensors. Milk helps because the stuff likes fat more than water. Water just moves it around.
why.try: Yogurt beats a glass of water. Science snack.
why.tryLine: Yogurt beats a glass of water. Science snack.

why.headline: Why can you feel a pulse?
why.summary: Each squeeze of the heart sends a pressure wave down your arteries. Fingers on a wrist catch the wave. That is not the heart itself in your wrist.
why.try: Find it on a parent, then on you after 20 star jumps.
why.tryLine: Find it on a parent, then on you after 20 star jumps.

why.headline: Why do we need sleep?
why.summary: Sleep is not off. The brain files memories, the body repairs, and junk gets cleared. Skip it and mood, memory, and aim all get worse.
why.try: Same bedtime most nights beats a giant weekend lie-in.
why.tryLine: Same bedtime most nights beats a giant weekend lie-in.

why.headline: Why do we dream?
why.summary: Nobody has the full map. The brain replays, mixes, and files the day. Dreams feel real because the same vision kit is running with the body parked.
why.try: Keep a 10-second dream note. Patterns show up.
why.tryLine: Keep a 10-second dream note. Patterns show up.

why.headline: Why do you forget why you walked in?
why.summary: Doorways help the brain dump the last room's plan. You start a hallway file. The mission falls out.
why.try: Say the job out loud before you move.
why.tryLine: Say the job out loud before you move.

why.headline: Why does practice actually work?
why.summary: Repeated tries build stronger paths in the brain. Mistakes are the map. Slow, focused reps beat zoned-out grinding.
why.try: Ten good tries beat fifty sloppy ones.
why.tryLine: Ten good tries beat fifty sloppy ones.

why.headline: Why does 'thank you' change a room?
why.summary: People want to know they landed. A specific thanks ('that pass was perfect') is jet fuel. It costs one second and buys a better next try from everyone.
why.try: Pick one person today. Name the exact thing.
why.tryLine: Pick one person today. Name the exact thing.

why.headline: Why don't we fall off a round Earth?
why.summary: Down means toward the middle. Everywhere on the ball, 'down' is inward. You are stuck by the same pull that holds the Moon in orbit.
why.try: Antipodes are not hanging off a ceiling. They have their own down.
why.tryLine: Antipodes are not hanging off a ceiling. They have their own down.

why.headline: Why is there day and night?
why.summary: Earth spins. Your bit turns toward the Sun (day) then away (night). One spin is about 24 hours.
why.try: A globe and a torch in a dark room. Instant planet.
why.tryLine: A globe and a torch in a dark room. Instant planet.

why.headline: Why do tides happen?
why.summary: The Moon's pull tugs the oceans into a bulge. Earth turns through that bulge. High tide, low tide. The Sun helps a bit too.
why.try: Check a tide app before a beach day.
why.tryLine: Check a tide app before a beach day.

why.headline: Why do auroras exist?
why.summary: The Sun throws charged particles. Earth's magnetic field funnels them to the poles. They smack air and the air glows green and pink.
why.try: Best near the Arctic or Antarctic. Not a UK every-night show.
why.tryLine: Best near the Arctic or Antarctic. Not a UK every-night show.

why.headline: Why is the Moon full of craters?
why.summary: No wind, no rain, no plate tectonics to erase scars. Rocks that hit stay written on the face. Earth gets hit too — weather deletes the evidence.
why.try: Binoculars on the Moon. Instant battlefield.
why.tryLine: Binoculars on the Moon. Instant battlefield.

why.headline: Why put a telescope in deep cold space?
why.summary: Heat is noise for infrared light. Webb sits far from Earth, behind a sunshade, ice-cold, so faint heat from baby galaxies can show up.
why.try: A warm camera in a bright room is the opposite of Webb.
why.tryLine: A warm camera in a bright room is the opposite of Webb.

why.headline: Why is plastic a sea problem?
why.summary: Plastic does not really go away. It breaks into bits fish mistake for food. Rivers are the conveyor belt from streets to ocean.
why.try: One bottle you don't drop is a fish that doesn't eat it.
why.tryLine: One bottle you don't drop is a fish that doesn't eat it.

why.headline: Why do bees matter so much?
why.summary: They move pollen so plants can make fruit and seeds. No bees, fewer apples, almonds, and wildflowers. A garden with mixed flowers is a bee cafe.
why.try: Plant one bee-friendly flower this year.
why.tryLine: Plant one bee-friendly flower this year.

why.headline: Do trees really 'talk'?
why.summary: Not with mouths. Roots and fungi share water, carbon, and warnings underground. A stressed tree can change what neighbours do. Slow chat, real science.
why.try: A forest is a network, not just a bunch of sticks.
why.tryLine: A forest is a network, not just a bunch of sticks.

why.headline: Why do canyons echo more?
why.summary: Hard rock walls, long gaps, less soft stuff to swallow sound. The clap comes home. Forests eat echoes. Cliffs send them back.
why.try: Clap on a path, then under a bridge.
why.tryLine: Clap on a path, then under a bridge.

why.headline: Why does camouflage work?
why.summary: Predators (and games) hunt with eyes first. Break the outline, match the background, stay still. Your brain likes edges. Hide the edges, hide the animal.
why.try: Spot the moth on bark. Then you can't unsee it.
why.tryLine: Spot the moth on bark. Then you can't unsee it.

why.headline: Why do zebras have stripes?
why.summary: Best evidence now: stripes mess with biting flies. Temperature and dazzle-to-lions are extra theories. Flies hate the pattern.
why.try: Nature's bug spray is a paint job.
why.tryLine: Nature's bug spray is a paint job.

why.headline: Why are giraffe tongues dark?
why.summary: Long tongues in harsh sun. Extra pigment may work like a built-in sunblock so they don't get tongue-sunburn picking leaves all day.
why.try: Imagine licking a tree for lunch. You'd want armour too.
why.tryLine: Imagine licking a tree for lunch. You'd want armour too.

why.headline: Why are owls silent in flight?
why.summary: Fringed feathers break the whoosh into soft turbulence. Prey hears nothing until it's late. Planes study this trick.
why.try: Listen to a pigeon take off. Then imagine the opposite.
why.tryLine: Listen to a pigeon take off. Then imagine the opposite.

why.headline: Why don't penguins' feet freeze?
why.summary: They use a heat-exchange trick: warm blood going down heats cold blood coming up. Feet stay just warm enough, body keeps the rest.
why.try: Wetsuit for the soul. Plumbing for the feet.
why.tryLine: Wetsuit for the soul. Plumbing for the feet.

why.headline: Why can camels go so long without water?
why.summary: They don't store it in the hump — that's fat. They handle huge body-temperature swings and drink a lot when they finally find a pool.
why.try: Hump = lunchbox, not water bottle.
why.tryLine: Hump = lunchbox, not water bottle.

why.headline: Why do paper cuts hurt so much?
why.summary: Fingertips are packed with nerves. Paper makes a shallow, messy cut that stays open and hits salt from sweat. Tiny wound, loud alarm.
why.try: Wash, then a plaster. Drama over.
why.tryLine: Wash, then a plaster. Drama over.

why.headline: Why do bruises change colour?
why.summary: Blood leaks under the skin, then your body recycles it. Purple, green, yellow is the cleanup playlist. Means healing is happening.
why.try: If a bruise keeps growing fast, tell a grown-up.
why.tryLine: If a bruise keeps growing fast, tell a grown-up.

why.headline: Why do scabs form?
why.summary: Blood nets itself into a plug, then dries. Underneath, new skin is being knitted. Pick it and you rip the building site.
why.try: Leave it. Ugly is useful.
why.tryLine: Leave it. Ugly is useful.

why.headline: Why do vaccines help?
why.summary: They show your immune system a safe wanted-poster of a germ. Next time the real germ shows up, your body already has the plan.
why.try: Not magic. Memory.
why.tryLine: Not magic. Memory.

why.headline: Why does soap beat germs?
why.summary: Soap is two-faced: one end loves water, one loves grease. It pries virus shells and dirt apart, then water rinses the bits away. Time plus bubbles.
why.try: 20 seconds. Sing a short chorus.
why.tryLine: 20 seconds. Sing a short chorus.

why.headline: Why does running change your mood?
why.summary: Bodies release chemicals that calm pain and lift mood. Breathing harder also burns leftover stress energy. Five minutes still counts.
why.try: Sprint to the end of the street. Notice the after.
why.tryLine: Sprint to the end of the street. Notice the after.

why.headline: Why do names fall out of your head?
why.summary: You heard it once, while thinking of your own hello. The brain filed nothing. Repeat + picture is a hook.
why.try: Say it back. Stick it to a silly image.
why.tryLine: Say it back. Stick it to a silly image.

why.headline: Why do game skills leak into real life?
why.summary: Aim, timing, planning, fail-and-retry. The brain reuses those loops. The trick is picking games that reward patience, not only rage.
why.try: After a fail in-game, name one thing you'll try different.
why.tryLine: After a fail in-game, name one thing you'll try different.

why.headline: Why is boredom useful?
why.summary: An empty minute is when the brain starts making its own fun. If a screen fills every gap, that muscle stays floppy.
why.try: Leave 10 minutes with no phone. See what idea shows up.
why.tryLine: Leave 10 minutes with no phone. See what idea shows up.

why.headline: Why do we have two eyes?
why.summary: Each eye sees a slightly different picture. The brain stacks them into depth, so you can tell near from far and catch a ball.
why.try: Close one eye and try to pinch a pencil point.
why.tryLine: Close one eye and try to pinch a pencil point.

why.headline: Why do we blink so much?
why.summary: A blink is a tiny wash and wipe. Tears spread, dust leaves, the eye stays clear. You do it without a meeting.
why.try: Try not to blink for 20 seconds. Notice the itch.
why.tryLine: Try not to blink for 20 seconds. Notice the itch.

why.headline: Why do we sneeze?
why.summary: Something tickles the nose. The body loads a blast of air to fire it out. Eyes close so the blast does not hit them.
why.try: Pepper is a classic trigger. Use a tiny pinch, then wash hands.
why.tryLine: Pepper is a classic trigger. Use a tiny pinch, then wash hands.

why.headline: Why do we have fingerprints?
why.summary: The ridges grip like tyre treads and help you feel tiny textures. They form before birth. Even twins do not match.
why.try: Press a finger on a glass. The print is oil, not ink.
why.tryLine: Press a finger on a glass. The print is oil, not ink.

why.headline: Why does ice cream give brain freeze?
why.summary: Cold hits the roof of the mouth. Nearby blood vessels slam shut, then open fast. The brain reads that rush as forehead pain.
why.try: Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Warmth ends it.
why.tryLine: Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Warmth ends it.

why.headline: Why do we get thirsty?
why.summary: Salt and water have a ratio. Too little water and sensors in the brain ring a bell. The dry mouth is the alarm, not the whole story.
why.try: After a run, sip. Gulping a litre at once is the panic version.
why.tryLine: After a run, sip. Gulping a litre at once is the panic version.

why.headline: Why do we get sunburned?
why.summary: Invisible UV light nicks DNA in skin cells. The body rushes blood and alarm chemicals. Red is the repair crew, not a tan in progress.
why.try: Shade plus sleeves beat a heroic burn.
why.tryLine: Shade plus sleeves beat a heroic burn.

why.headline: Why do we get dizzy after spinning?
why.summary: Fluid in your inner ear keeps spinning after you stop. The eyes say 'still'. The brain believes both and the room tilts.
why.try: Spin, stop, stare at one far thing. The fluid catches up.
why.tryLine: Spin, stop, stare at one far thing. The fluid catches up.

why.headline: Why do you get a stitch when you run?
why.summary: A sharp side pain often comes from the diaphragm cramping, plus a jiggling gut. Slow the breath. It usually backs off.
why.try: Walk 30 seconds, breathe out long. Then jog again.
why.tryLine: Walk 30 seconds, breathe out long. Then jog again.

why.headline: Why do we get pins and needles?
why.summary: Sit on a nerve or squeeze a blood path and the signal goes fuzzy. When it wakes, the nerve fires junk — that tingle is the reboot.
why.try: Stand up and shake the foot. Do not wait it out on the nerve.
why.tryLine: Stand up and shake the foot. Do not wait it out on the nerve.

why.headline: Why do we blush?
why.summary: Embarrassment opens face blood vessels. You cannot decide to blush. Other people see you know the moment mattered.
why.try: Next time it happens, name it: that's blood, not a fail.
why.tryLine: Next time it happens, name it: that's blood, not a fail.

why.headline: Why do we have two nostrils?
why.summary: They take turns being the main airway. One swells a bit, the other stays open. Smell also needs a slow lane and a fast lane.
why.try: Cover one side, then the other. One feels easier.
why.tryLine: Cover one side, then the other. One feels easier.

why.headline: Why do we have eyebrows?
why.summary: They are sweat gutters and tiny signal flags. Rain and sweat get steered sideways. A raised brow says more than a paragraph.
why.try: Raise just one. That's a skill some brains skip.
why.tryLine: Raise just one. That's a skill some brains skip.

why.headline: Why do we have a belly button?
why.summary: Before you breathed air, a cord brought food and oxygen from your parent. The scar is the closed door. Innie or outie is just how it healed.
why.try: It is not a hole into your insides. It is a sealed scar.
why.tryLine: It is not a hole into your insides. It is a sealed scar.

why.headline: Why do we laugh?
why.summary: Laugh is a social signal more than a joke detector. Groups use it to say 'we are safe together'. That is why laugh tracks exist.
why.try: Watch someone laugh at a tiny thing with a friend. The friend is the point.
why.tryLine: Watch someone laugh at a tiny thing with a friend. The friend is the point.

why.headline: Why do we have earwax?
why.summary: It is sticky armour. Dust, bugs, and dry skin get trapped and walk out on their own. Cotton buds shove the mess deeper.
why.try: Leave it. A washcloth on the outer ear is enough.
why.tryLine: Leave it. A washcloth on the outer ear is enough.

why.headline: Why do we have fingernails?
why.summary: The hard plate lets you pick, peel, and scratch with precision. It also backs the fingertip so touch is sharper.
why.try: Try opening a snack packet with no nails. Instant respect.
why.tryLine: Try opening a snack packet with no nails. Instant respect.

why.headline: Why does metal feel colder than wood?
why.summary: Room temperature is the same. Metal steals heat from your hand faster. Wood is a poor thief, so it feels friendlier.
why.try: Touch a spoon and a wooden table. Same room, different steal.
why.tryLine: Touch a spoon and a wooden table. Same room, different steal.

why.headline: Why can you see your breath in winter?
why.summary: Warm wet air from your lungs hits cold air and the water becomes tiny droplets. A personal cloud. Same idea as fog.
why.try: Breathe on a cold window. That's the cloud sitting down.
why.tryLine: Breathe on a cold window. That's the cloud sitting down.

why.headline: Why do windows fog up?
why.summary: Warm indoor air holds more water. Hit cold glass and the water has to leave as droplets. Fog is weather on a pane.
why.try: A tiny gap of air or a wipe changes the surface.
why.tryLine: A tiny gap of air or a wipe changes the surface.

why.headline: Why do fizzy drinks fizz?
why.summary: The bottle is packed with carbon dioxide under pressure. Open it and the gas races out as bubbles. Warmth and shaking make more leave at once.
why.try: Open a warm shaken bottle outside. Science, and a mess.
why.tryLine: Open a warm shaken bottle outside. Science, and a mess.

why.headline: Why does a straw 'suck'?
why.summary: You lower the pressure in your mouth. Air pressure on the drink is now stronger, so it pushes the liquid up the straw. You do not pull water. Air pushes it.
why.try: Try a straw with a hole in the side. The push leaks.
why.tryLine: Try a straw with a hole in the side. The push leaks.

why.headline: Why do rubber balls bounce?
why.summary: The ball squashes and stores the hit as spring. Then it shoves the ground back. A bit of energy becomes heat, so each bounce is smaller.
why.try: A flat ball has no spring left. Pump it.
why.tryLine: A flat ball has no spring left. Pump it.

why.headline: Why does a plane leave a white trail?
why.summary: Hot wet exhaust hits cold thin air and water freezes into a cloud behind the engines. Wind smears it. Not smoke.
why.try: If the trail vanishes fast, the air up there is dry.
why.tryLine: If the trail vanishes fast, the air up there is dry.

why.headline: Why does a moving bike stay up?
why.summary: Speed plus tiny steering corrections keep the wheels under you. A parked bike has no corrections. Magic is just fast balance.
why.try: Ride slow in a straight line. Harder than fast.
why.tryLine: Ride slow in a straight line. Harder than fast.

why.headline: Why is the sea salty?
why.summary: Rivers carry tiny bits of rock salt to the ocean. Water leaves as rain. Salt stays. Billions of years of that and you get brine.
why.try: A splash that dries on skin feels dusty. That's the leftover.
why.tryLine: A splash that dries on skin feels dusty. That's the leftover.

why.headline: Why do leaves change colour?
why.summary: Green is chlorophyll, the food factory. In autumn some trees shut it down and store the good stuff. Yellow and orange were there all year, hiding.
why.try: Hold a yellow leaf to the light. The veins still show the old plan.
why.tryLine: Hold a yellow leaf to the light. The veins still show the old plan.

why.headline: Why is grass green?
why.summary: Chlorophyll is great at grabbing red and blue light for food. It shrugs at green, so green bounces into your eyes.
why.try: A dying lawn goes yellow when the factory shuts.
why.tryLine: A dying lawn goes yellow when the factory shuts.

why.headline: Why does iron rust?
why.summary: Iron likes oxygen more than it likes being a nail. Water helps the swap. The orange flake is iron giving up electrons.
why.try: A dry bike rusts slower. Wipe it.
why.tryLine: A dry bike rusts slower. Wipe it.

why.headline: Why do cats often land on their feet?
why.summary: A cat can twist its spine in two halves, then the tail helps the last turn. They still get hurt from high places. Superpower, not a force field.
why.try: Do not test this. Believe the videos that already exist.
why.tryLine: Do not test this. Believe the videos that already exist.

why.headline: Why do birds fly in a V?
why.summary: Each bird rides a bit of lift from the one in front, like drafting on bikes. The lead bird works hardest, so they swap.
why.try: Watch geese. The V wiggles when someone takes a turn.
why.tryLine: Watch geese. The V wiggles when someone takes a turn.

why.headline: Why do ants walk in a line?
why.summary: A finder lays a scent trail home. Others follow and thicken the smell. No boss. Just a smell that got popular.
why.try: Wipe a tiny gap in a trail with a finger. Watch the confusion, then the rebuild.
why.tryLine: Wipe a tiny gap in a trail with a finger. Watch the confusion, then the rebuild.

why.headline: Why do fireflies glow?
why.summary: A chemical reaction in the tail makes cold light. They use it to say 'hello, same species' and sometimes 'do not eat me'.
why.try: If you ever catch one, a jar with air holes, then let it go.
why.tryLine: If you ever catch one, a jar with air holes, then let it go.

why.headline: Why do snakes stick out their tongue?
why.summary: The tongue grabs a sample of air and parks it on a smell organ in the mouth. A fork means left-and-right, so they can follow a trail.
why.try: It is tasting the room, not being rude.
why.tryLine: It is tasting the room, not being rude.

why.headline: Why do bats hang upside down?
why.summary: Their feet lock when they relax, so hanging is the cheap rest. Taking off from a hang is easier than a standing jump for those wings.
why.try: A bat on the ground is having a bad day. Give it space.
why.tryLine: A bat on the ground is having a bad day. Give it space.

why.headline: Why don't ducks get soaked?
why.summary: Oil from a gland near the tail, plus dense feathers, makes water bead and roll off. A duck preens to spread the raincoat.
why.try: Watch a duck after a dive. A shake, then dry-looking again.
why.tryLine: Watch a duck after a dive. A shake, then dry-looking again.

why.headline: Why do bees dance?
why.summary: A waggle run inside the dark hive points to food. Angle versus the sun, length of the waggle for distance. GPS made of wriggle.
why.try: No playlist. The dance is the map.
why.tryLine: No playlist. The dance is the map.

why.headline: Why do we have time zones?
why.summary: Noon should be when the sun is high. Earth is a ball, so 'high' happens at different clock times. Zones are a truce so noon is roughly noon.
why.try: Call someone far west. Their lunch is your evening.
why.tryLine: Call someone far west. Their lunch is your evening.

why.headline: Why is a year about 365 days?
why.summary: That is how long Earth takes to go once around the Sun. The extra quarter-day is why leap years exist. The planet does not care about calendars.
why.try: Your birthday is one lap.
why.tryLine: Your birthday is one lap.

why.headline: Why is a week seven days?
why.summary: Not a planet fact. People picked seven a long time ago — moon phases, old sky gods — and it stuck. Months follow the Moon more closely.
why.try: A five-day week would also work. Habit won.
why.tryLine: A five-day week would also work. Habit won.

why.headline: Why does waiting feel longer than it is?
why.summary: A bored brain checks the clock. Each check makes a new memory of 'still waiting'. Busy brains file fewer of those, so time feels shorter.
why.try: Next queue, count red things. The clock gets quieter.
why.tryLine: Next queue, count red things. The clock gets quieter.

why.headline: Why does a song get stuck in your head?
why.summary: A short loop with no ending keeps the brain trying to 'finish' it. Simple hooks win. It is a puzzle, not a haunting.
why.try: Play the song to the real end, or swap in a different chorus.
why.tryLine: Play the song to the real end, or swap in a different chorus.

why.headline: Why do we copy our friends?
why.summary: Brains save work by borrowing what nearby people do. It helps you belong. It can also walk you into a dumb idea as a group.
why.try: Before a copy, ask: do I want this, or do I want them?
why.tryLine: Before a copy, ask: do I want this, or do I want them?

why.headline: Why do rumours travel faster than facts?
why.summary: A juicy maybe feels useful and is easy to retell. Facts are often boring and have names attached. Speed loves simple and spicy.
why.try: Before you pass it on, ask who saw it.
why.tryLine: Before you pass it on, ask who saw it.

why.headline: Why does jet lag exist?
why.summary: Your body clock is set by light at home. Fly far and the sun disagrees. Sleep, hunger, and mood take a few days to believe the new sky.
why.try: Morning light in the new place is the reset button.
why.tryLine: Morning light in the new place is the reset button.

why.headline: Why do pupils get bigger in the dark?
why.summary: The iris is a muscle ring. In dim light it opens so more photons can hit the retina. Bright light slams it shut to protect the sensors.
why.try: Watch a pupil in a mirror, then flick a light on.
why.tryLine: Watch a pupil in a mirror, then flick a light on.

why.headline: Why does each eye have a blind spot?
why.summary: The optic nerve punches through the retina, so no photoreceptors sit there. Two eyes overlap, so the brain paints over the hole.
why.try: Close one eye and slide a finger across your view. A bit vanishes.
why.tryLine: Close one eye and slide a finger across your view. A bit vanishes.

why.headline: Why do you see a glow after a camera flash?
why.summary: Bright light bleaches pigments in the retina. Until they reload, that patch reports the opposite colour. That leftover report is the afterimage.
why.try: Stare at a bright logo, then look at a white wall.
why.tryLine: Stare at a bright logo, then look at a white wall.

why.headline: Why do you notice motion at the edge of your eye first?
why.summary: Edge vision is packed with motion detectors, not fine detail. It is a burglar alarm, not a book.
why.try: Wave a hand at the side of your head without looking.
why.tryLine: Wave a hand at the side of your head without looking.

why.headline: Why do 3D glasses make a screen jump out?
why.summary: Each lens feeds one eye a slightly different picture. The brain stacks them into depth, the same trick two eyes use in real life.
why.try: Take the glasses off mid-film. The double image is the secret.
why.tryLine: Take the glasses off mid-film. The double image is the secret.

why.headline: Why do some pictures look like they move?
why.summary: High-contrast repeats fool motion detectors. The eyes micro-saccade and the brain reads that jitter as movement.
why.try: Hold still and the 'motion' often dies down.
why.tryLine: Hold still and the 'motion' often dies down.

why.headline: Why do some people sneeze at bright sun?
why.summary: A bright blast can tickle the same nerve that runs the sneeze reflex. Not an allergy. A crossed wire.
why.try: Step from shade to sun and notice if a sneeze comes.
why.tryLine: Step from shade to sun and notice if a sneeze comes.

why.headline: Why does a cold make your nose run?
why.summary: Viruses irritate the lining. Extra mucus flushes them out. The drip is the clean-up crew, messy on purpose.
why.try: A tissue is the crew's exit door.
why.tryLine: A tissue is the crew's exit door.

why.headline: Why do we get a fever?
why.summary: The body turns the thermostat up. Many germs copy themselves worse in the heat. You feel awful because the factory is on overtime.
why.try: Rest and water help the factory. Don't 'fight' a mild fever for sport.
why.tryLine: Rest and water help the factory. Don't 'fight' a mild fever for sport.

why.headline: Why does sweat start to smell?
why.summary: Fresh sweat is mostly water. Skin bacteria eat the leftover oils and burp out the pong.
why.try: Wash the places bacteria throw a party.
why.tryLine: Wash the places bacteria throw a party.

why.headline: Why does sweat taste salty?
why.summary: Sweat carries salt out with the water. The body is dumping heat, and some minerals hitch a ride.
why.try: After a hot day, lips can taste like the sea.
why.tryLine: After a hot day, lips can taste like the sea.

why.headline: Why does cold air give you bumps?
why.summary: Tiny muscles lift each hair. In furry ancestors that trapped a warm layer. On us it is a leftover salute.
why.try: Look at an arm after a cold drink.
why.tryLine: Look at an arm after a cold drink.

why.headline: Why do we shiver?
why.summary: Muscles twitch on purpose. Twitching burns fuel and makes heat. It is a built-in space heater.
why.try: Move around. Bigger motion makes more heat than a shiver.
why.tryLine: Move around. Bigger motion makes more heat than a shiver.

why.headline: Why do teeth chatter when you are cold?
why.summary: The jaw is a muscle too. The same shiver program rattles it.
why.try: A scarf on the neck calms the thermostat.
why.tryLine: A scarf on the neck calms the thermostat.

why.headline: Why can lips look blue in the cold?
why.summary: Cold shrinks blood vessels near the skin. Less red blood shows, so the tissue looks bluish.
why.try: Warm hands first. Colour comes back with blood.
why.tryLine: Warm hands first. Colour comes back with blood.

why.headline: Why is a breath-cloud thicker on some days?
why.summary: Colder, stiller air turns more of your moisture into droplets. Wind rips the cloud apart.
why.try: Compare a frosty morning with a windy one.
why.tryLine: Compare a frosty morning with a windy one.

why.headline: Why do ears pop on a hill?
why.summary: Air pressure outside changes faster than the air in the middle ear. The tube to your throat opens with a swallow and equalises.
why.try: Yawn or swallow on purpose.
why.tryLine: Yawn or swallow on purpose.

why.headline: Why do ears hurt more on the way down in a plane?
why.summary: Descent raises outside pressure. The eardrum gets pushed in until the tube opens.
why.try: Sip or chew on descent, not just takeoff.
why.tryLine: Sip or chew on descent, not just takeoff.

why.headline: Why does yawning help on a plane?
why.summary: A yawn tugs the tube to the middle ear open. Pressure evens out. The yawn is a tool, not boredom.
why.try: Fake a yawn. It still works.
why.tryLine: Fake a yawn. It still works.

why.headline: Why does reading in a car make some people sick?
why.summary: Eyes say 'still page'. Inner ear says 'moving box'. The brain hates the argument and throws a warning.
why.try: Look at the horizon. Give both sensors the same story.
why.tryLine: Look at the horizon. Give both sensors the same story.

why.headline: Why does a spinning chair wreck you?
why.summary: Fluid in the inner ear keeps moving after you stop. Eyes say stop. The mismatch is nausea.
why.try: Stare at one far point after you spin.
why.tryLine: Stare at one far point after you spin.

why.headline: Why can a headset make you queasy?
why.summary: The picture moves. Your body does not. Same argument as a car, in goggles.
why.try: Sit for the first minutes. Let the brain catch up.
why.tryLine: Sit for the first minutes. Let the brain catch up.

why.headline: Why does an arm 'fall asleep'?
why.summary: Pressure pinches a nerve or a blood path. Signals go fuzzy. Pins and needles are the reboot.
why.try: Move it. Do not wait on the nerve.
why.tryLine: Move it. Do not wait on the nerve.

why.headline: Why does the funny bone feel electric?
why.summary: It is the ulnar nerve, not a bone. A knock zaps it against the elbow. The tingle runs the nerve's whole map.
why.try: Rub it. The map fades.
why.tryLine: Rub it. The map fades.

why.headline: Why do you feel a funny-bone zap in the fingers?
why.summary: The nerve that got hit also serves the ring and little fingers. The message uses that wire.
why.try: Wiggle those two fingers after a knock.
why.tryLine: Wiggle those two fingers after a knock.

why.headline: Why does a lift give a stomach-drop?
why.summary: For a second you and your guts accelerate differently. Sensors shout 'falling'.
why.try: Knees soft. The shout is brief.
why.tryLine: Knees soft. The shout is brief.

why.headline: Why does a scare make you fast and shaky?
why.summary: Adrenaline dumps fuel into blood, opens airways, and turns down pain. Shake is leftover charge.
why.try: Walk it off. The charge wants a job.
why.tryLine: Walk it off. The charge wants a job.

why.headline: Why does a fright speed up your heart?
why.summary: Faster beats push blood to muscles. The body is betting you might run.
why.try: Breathe out long. That is the stand-down signal.
why.tryLine: Breathe out long. That is the stand-down signal.

why.headline: Why does your mouth go dry before a talk?
why.summary: The fight-or-flight switch parks digestion, including spit. You are not thirsty. You are primed.
why.try: Sip water. It is a prop and a reset.
why.tryLine: Sip water. It is a prop and a reset.

why.headline: Why do nerves sit in the stomach?
why.summary: The gut has its own nerve net. Stress chemicals hit it. Flutter is real traffic, not a metaphor.
why.try: Eat light before a big thing.
why.tryLine: Eat light before a big thing.

why.headline: Why does a blush feel hot?
why.summary: Face vessels open. Extra blood is heat you can feel from the inside.
why.try: Name it: that's blood, not a fail.
why.tryLine: Name it: that's blood, not a fail.

why.headline: Why do we cry when we are sad?
why.summary: Tears are a social signal and a chemical dump. The face scrunch is the same kit as pain.
why.try: A cry that ends often leaves the body quieter.
why.tryLine: A cry that ends often leaves the body quieter.

why.headline: Why are onion tears different from sad tears?
why.summary: Onion gas stings the eye. The gland flushes it. Sad tears carry extra hormones. Same tap, different reason.
why.try: Step back from the board. Air helps the sting ones.
why.tryLine: Step back from the board. Air helps the sting ones.

why.headline: Why can a huge laugh make you cry?
why.summary: The same overflow valve pops. Face muscles squeeze the gland.
why.try: It is not sadness sneaking in. It is plumbing.
why.tryLine: It is not sadness sneaking in. It is plumbing.

why.headline: Why can a scare stop hiccups?
why.summary: A jolt can reset the spasm loop in the diaphragm. Not magic. A reboot.
why.try: A sudden swallow of water is a gentler reboot.
why.tryLine: A sudden swallow of water is a gentler reboot.

why.headline: Why do we burp?
why.summary: Swallowed air and gas from the gut need an exit. The valve at the stomach burps them out.
why.try: Slow drinks make fewer guests.
why.tryLine: Slow drinks make fewer guests.

why.headline: Why do beans make more gas?
why.summary: Some sugars we cannot break. Gut microbes can, and they burp methane and pals.
why.try: The sound is the exit. The smell is the menu.
why.tryLine: The sound is the exit. The smell is the menu.

why.headline: Why does one yawn start a chain in a room?
why.summary: Brains copy nearby bodies. A yawn is a strong copy-me signal. It may also cool the brain a bit.
why.try: Notice who yawns next. You are watching a network.
why.tryLine: Notice who yawns next. You are watching a network.

why.headline: Why do we stretch after sleep?
why.summary: Muscles sat still. A stretch wakes sensors and pushes blood through. Cats have the right idea.
why.try: Do one slow reach before the phone.
why.tryLine: Do one slow reach before the phone.

why.headline: Why can a leg cramp at night?
why.summary: A muscle fires and forgets to stop. Tiredness, salt, or a pointed-toe stretch can trip it.
why.try: Pull the toes toward you. That fights the cramp.
why.tryLine: Pull the toes toward you. That fights the cramp.

why.headline: Why a stitch after lunch-and-run?
why.summary: A full gut plus bouncing organs plus a working diaphragm. The side grab is a protest.
why.try: Walk, breathe out long, then jog.
why.tryLine: Walk, breathe out long, then jog.

why.headline: Why do you sometimes get a second wind?
why.summary: Breathing and blood flow catch up. Early panic chemicals fade. The engine finds a gear.
why.try: The first five minutes are the lie.
why.tryLine: The first five minutes are the lie.

why.headline: Why do muscles burn in a sprint?
why.summary: They make energy without enough oxygen for a bit. Acid and other leftovers sting. The burn is a speed limit.
why.try: Ease off. The cleanup crew is coming.
why.tryLine: Ease off. The cleanup crew is coming.

why.headline: Why are you more sore the next day?
why.summary: Tiny muscle damage plus the repair swell. The delay is the immune crew arriving late.
why.try: Gentle movement helps more than a sofa.
why.tryLine: Gentle movement helps more than a sofa.

why.headline: Why do old scars look paler?
why.summary: Scar tissue has a different collagen weave and fewer pigment cells. Light bounces differently.
why.try: It is a patch, not the original cloth.
why.tryLine: It is a patch, not the original cloth.

why.headline: Why does a bruise go yellow?
why.summary: Blood under the skin breaks down. The colours are the leftover pigments in order.
why.try: Yellow means the cleanup is late-stage.
why.tryLine: Yellow means the cleanup is late-stage.

why.headline: Why does a healing cut itch?
why.summary: Nerves grow back into the repair. Histamine from the crew adds an itch signal.
why.try: Do not rip the scab. That resets the job.
why.tryLine: Do not rip the scab. That resets the job.

why.headline: Why do tight shoes make a blister?
why.summary: Rub separates skin layers. Fluid fills the gap as a cushion. The bubble is a built-in bandage.
why.try: Leave a clean blister closed if you can.
why.tryLine: Leave a clean blister closed if you can.

why.headline: Why do hands grow thicker skin?
why.summary: Repeat pressure tells skin to stack extra layers. A callus is a homemade glove.
why.try: The first week of a new tool is the tender week.
why.tryLine: The first week of a new tool is the tender week.

why.headline: Why does sunburned skin peel?
why.summary: UV-killed cells get evicted in sheets. The peel is the demolition, not a tan arriving.
why.try: Next time: shade. Peeling is the bill.
why.tryLine: Next time: shade. Peeling is the bill.

why.headline: Why do some people freckle?
why.summary: Extra pigment clumps where sun hits. The clumps are umbrellas that did not spread evenly.
why.try: They are common. They are not dirt.
why.tryLine: They are common. They are not dirt.

why.headline: Why does skin tan?
why.summary: UV tells pigment cells to make more melanin. The brown is a shield, late to the party.
why.try: A tan still means damage already happened.
why.tryLine: A tan still means damage already happened.

why.headline: Why do we have moles?
why.summary: A cluster of pigment cells grew in one spot. Most are harmless maps.
why.try: A grown-up checks ones that change.
why.tryLine: A grown-up checks ones that change.

why.headline: Why does hair go grey?
why.summary: Pigment factories in the follicle retire. The hair still grows. It just forgot colour.
why.try: Grey is a timeline, not a stain.
why.tryLine: Grey is a timeline, not a stain.

why.headline: Why does a scary film lift your hair?
why.summary: The same tiny muscles as goosebumps. Ancestors looked bigger. You look slightly electric.
why.try: It fades when the scene does.
why.tryLine: It fades when the scene does.

why.headline: Why does the scalp flake?
why.summary: Skin there turns over fast. Oil plus yeast plus dry air can clump the flakes.
why.try: A wash beats a scratch.
why.tryLine: A wash beats a scratch.

why.headline: Why is earwax yellow-brown?
why.summary: It is oil, dead skin, and dust cooked together. The colour is the mix, not an infection by itself.
why.try: Leave the canal alone.
why.tryLine: Leave the canal alone.

why.headline: Why is there crust in the eyes in the morning?
why.summary: Tears and oil dry at the corners while you sleep. The crust is leftover weather.
why.try: Warm water. Not a fingernail.
why.tryLine: Warm water. Not a fingernail.

why.headline: Why do people say 'sleep sand'?
why.summary: The dried tear-oil bits look like grains. Same stuff as the crust.
why.try: It is not beach sand. Do not invent lore.
why.tryLine: It is not beach sand. Do not invent lore.

why.headline: Why do some people drool in sleep?
why.summary: The swallow reflex naps. Gravity plus an open mouth does the rest.
why.try: Side sleeping changes the drip path.
why.tryLine: Side sleeping changes the drip path.

why.headline: Why do people snore?
why.summary: Air rattles floppy tissue in the throat. Narrower path, louder rattle.
why.try: A nudge onto the side often quiets it.
why.tryLine: A nudge onto the side often quiets it.

why.headline: Why do people talk in their sleep?
why.summary: Speech circuits fire while the rest of the brain is offline. The sentences are leftover scraps.
why.try: Do not treat it as a secret confession.
why.tryLine: Do not treat it as a secret confession.

why.headline: Why can a body walk while the mind sleeps?
why.summary: Movement circuits wake. The thinking layer does not. The walker is on autopilot.
why.try: Clear the floor. That is the help.
why.tryLine: Clear the floor. That is the help.

why.headline: Why do most dreams vanish by breakfast?
why.summary: The brain does not file them like daytime memories. Unless you replay one, it evaporates.
why.try: Write one line if you want to keep it.
why.tryLine: Write one line if you want to keep it.

why.headline: Why do nightmares feel so real?
why.summary: Emotion centres are loud. Logic is quiet. The story has no editor.
why.try: A light and a drink of water break the spell.
why.tryLine: A light and a drink of water break the spell.

why.headline: Why can a kid scream but not wake?
why.summary: A different kind of night event. The body is alarmed; the mind is not in the room.
why.try: Quiet presence. Do not force a quiz.
why.tryLine: Quiet presence. Do not force a quiz.

why.headline: Why do kids need more sleep than grown-ups?
why.summary: Brains and bones are still building. Sleep is the construction shift.
why.try: Protect the shift. It is not laziness.
why.tryLine: Protect the shift. It is not laziness.

why.headline: Why do people say you grow in your sleep?
why.summary: Growth hormone pulses more at night. The saying is half true.
why.try: Food plus sleep is the real pair.
why.tryLine: Food plus sleep is the real pair.

why.headline: Why does being ill make you sleepy?
why.summary: Immune chemicals are also sleep chemicals. The body shuts the shop to fight.
why.try: Let it. That is the point.
why.tryLine: Let it. That is the point.

why.headline: Why does a busy mind block sleep?
why.summary: Alert circuits stay on. The bed becomes a thinking chair.
why.try: A boring paper book is a dimmer switch.
why.tryLine: A boring paper book is a dimmer switch.

why.headline: Why does counting sheep even exist?
why.summary: A dull loop occupies the chatter. Any boring sequence can do it.
why.try: Count breaths. Same trick, no farm.
why.tryLine: Count breaths. Same trick, no farm.

why.headline: Why does a pillow get hot?
why.summary: Your head dumps heat. Foam traps it. The pillow is a hat you forgot.
why.try: Flip it. The cool side is just unused air.
why.tryLine: Flip it. The cool side is just unused air.

why.headline: Why do some people kick the duvet off?
why.summary: The body overheats mid-sleep and votes with the legs.
why.try: A thinner layer stops the vote.
why.tryLine: A thinner layer stops the vote.

why.headline: Why do you wake thirsty?
why.summary: Mouth breathing dries you. Or supper was salty. The alarm is local.
why.try: A sip. A gallon at 2am is the panic version.
why.tryLine: A sip. A gallon at 2am is the panic version.

why.headline: Why more wee at night sometimes?
why.summary: Cool rooms, extra drinks, or a brain that did not issue the 'hold' hormone well.
why.try: Less before bed. Easy rule.
why.tryLine: Less before bed. Easy rule.

why.headline: Why is a morning voice gravelly?
why.summary: Tissues are puffy from lying down. Mucus sat still. The first words clear the pipes.
why.try: A hum warms them faster than a shout.
why.tryLine: A hum warms them faster than a shout.

why.headline: Why is morning breath worse?
why.summary: Saliva took the night off. Bacteria had hours with no rinse.
why.try: Brush. The night shift is over.
why.tryLine: Brush. The night shift is over.

why.headline: Why are eyes puffy in the morning?
why.summary: Fluid pools in the face while you lie flat. Standing drains it.
why.try: Give it twenty minutes of gravity.
why.tryLine: Give it twenty minutes of gravity.

why.headline: Why does one side of the hair go flat?
why.summary: You slept on it. Hair is a fibre. Pressure sets a crease.
why.try: Water plus fingers beat a fight.
why.tryLine: Water plus fingers beat a fight.

why.headline: Why does dry hair stick to a jumper?
why.summary: Electrons hop on. Hair and wool disagree about charge. They cling.
why.try: A little water or a metal comb calms it.
why.tryLine: A little water or a metal comb calms it.

why.headline: Why does a hat wreck a haircut?
why.summary: Heat plus pressure plus a new part-line. Hair remembers the hat more than the comb.
why.try: Let it cool before the next photo.
why.tryLine: Let it cool before the next photo.

why.headline: Why do hair ends split?
why.summary: The tip is the oldest part. The oil from the scalp never arrived. The fibre frays.
why.try: A trim removes the fray. Oil cannot glue it.
why.tryLine: A trim removes the fray. Oil cannot glue it.

why.headline: Why do fingernails grow faster than toenails?
why.summary: Hands get more blood and more knocks. Use speeds the factory.
why.try: Fingers win the race. Toes take months.
why.tryLine: Fingers win the race. Toes take months.

why.headline: Why white dots on nails?
why.summary: Usually a bump to the root weeks ago. The dot is a scar riding out.
why.try: It grows off. Not a calcium myth.
why.tryLine: It grows off. Not a calcium myth.

why.headline: Why do hangnails hurt so much?
why.summary: A tiny tear in living skin, packed with nerves, at a hinge you use all day.
why.try: Clip, do not peel. Peeling lengthens the tear.
why.tryLine: Clip, do not peel. Peeling lengthens the tear.

why.headline: Why is nail-biting hard to stop?
why.summary: It is a loop: itch, bite, short relief, repeat. The mouth is a built-in tool.
why.try: A bitter coat breaks the first half of the loop.
why.tryLine: A bitter coat breaks the first half of the loop.

why.headline: Why do first teeth get wobbly?
why.summary: Adult teeth push from below. The baby roots dissolve. Wobble is the eviction.
why.try: Wiggle gently. The tooth knows the date.
why.tryLine: Wiggle gently. The tooth knows the date.

why.headline: Why are late teeth called wisdom teeth?
why.summary: They arrive when you are older, supposedly wiser. The name is a joke that stuck.
why.try: Not everyone has room. That is a dentist chapter.
why.tryLine: Not everyone has room. That is a dentist chapter.

why.headline: Why do sweets help holes in teeth?
why.summary: Sugar feeds mouth bacteria. They make acid. Acid carves enamel.
why.try: A rinse after sweets beats a lecture.
why.tryLine: A rinse after sweets beats a lecture.

why.headline: Why does toothpaste talk about fluoride?
why.summary: It helps enamel rebuild after acid attacks. A mineral ally.
why.try: A pea-size blob is the dose.
why.tryLine: A pea-size blob is the dose.

why.headline: Why can braces move teeth?
why.summary: Slow steady pressure tells bone to rebuild. Teeth ride the rebuild.
why.try: It is months of tiny moves, not a yank.
why.tryLine: It is months of tiny moves, not a yank.

why.headline: Why a retainer after braces?
why.summary: Teeth remember the old address. The retainer is a bouncer at the new one.
why.try: Nights matter more than you think.
why.tryLine: Nights matter more than you think.

why.headline: Why does ice cream zing a tooth?
why.summary: Thinned enamel or a tiny crack lets cold hit the nerve highway.
why.try: The zing is a map. Tell a dentist the street.
why.tryLine: The zing is a map. Tell a dentist the street.

why.headline: Why does burnt-tongue food taste dull?
why.summary: The taste buds on top got cooked. They grow back in days.
why.try: Bland food is not your imagination.
why.tryLine: Bland food is not your imagination.

why.headline: Why does hot sauce make you sweat?
why.summary: The burn receptors also run the heat alarm. The body opens the sprinklers.
why.try: Yogurt cools better than water.
why.tryLine: Yogurt cools better than water.

why.headline: Why brain-freeze hits the forehead?
why.summary: Cold on the palate slams nearby vessels. The brain reads that as forehead pain.
why.try: Tongue to the roof. Warmth ends it.
why.tryLine: Tongue to the roof. Warmth ends it.

why.headline: Why does fizz sting the nose?
why.summary: Bubbles pop and tickle the same nerves as mustard. Carbon dioxide is a prankster.
why.try: Small sips. The prank is dose-dependent.
why.tryLine: Small sips. The prank is dose-dependent.

why.headline: Why does mustard go up your nose?
why.summary: A vapour rides the back of the throat into the nose. Eyes water as a bonus.
why.try: It fades fast. Wasabi uses the same trick.
why.tryLine: It fades fast. Wasabi uses the same trick.

why.headline: Why is wasabi a head-hit, not a tongue-hit?
why.summary: The burn is vapour, not oil. It storms the nose, then leaves.
why.try: Breathe out through the mouth.
why.tryLine: Breathe out through the mouth.

why.headline: Why does pepper make you sneeze?
why.summary: Fine dust tickles the sneeze wires. The blast is meant to clear the dust.
why.try: A tiny pinch is plenty for the demo.
why.tryLine: A tiny pinch is plenty for the demo.

why.headline: Why a fizzy-sweet rush then a slump?
why.summary: Fast sugar hits the blood, then the body overcorrects. Mood follows the curve.
why.try: Pair sweet with something slower.
why.tryLine: Pair sweet with something slower.

why.headline: Why do people get 'hangry'?
why.summary: Low fuel plus stress chemicals. The brain treats hunger like a threat.
why.try: A snack is conflict resolution.
why.tryLine: A snack is conflict resolution.

why.headline: Why is a growl louder in a test?
why.summary: An empty gut plus a quiet room. The same rumble exists at lunch. You just have an audience.
why.try: Everyone's gut has a band.
why.tryLine: Everyone's gut has a band.

why.headline: Why do salty crisps make you thirsty?
why.summary: Blood gets a bit saltier. Sensors demand water to dilute.
why.try: That is the point of the crisp.
why.tryLine: That is the point of the crisp.

why.headline: Why a dry mouth on a long run?
why.summary: Breathing hard through the mouth evaporates spit. Not always true thirst.
why.try: Sip. Do not chug a lake.
why.tryLine: Sip. Do not chug a lake.

why.headline: Why can a big cold drink cramp a run?
why.summary: A cold load in the gut plus bouncing. The diaphragm complains.
why.try: Small sips while moving.
why.tryLine: Small sips while moving.

why.headline: Why a dead arm after side-sleeping?
why.summary: You slept on the nerve. Same as the school-desk arm.
why.try: Roll. Shake. Do not panic.
why.tryLine: Roll. Shake. Do not panic.

why.headline: Why a crick from a weird pillow?
why.summary: A joint sat at a rude angle for hours. The morning turn is the bill.
why.try: Slow circles beat a sudden wrench.
why.tryLine: Slow circles beat a sudden wrench.

why.headline: Why does a jaw click?
why.summary: A little disc in the joint slips and pops back. Often harmless.
why.try: Do not turn it into a party trick.
why.tryLine: Do not turn it into a party trick.

why.headline: Why do knuckles crack?
why.summary: A bubble forms in the joint fluid and collapses. The gap needs time to reload.
why.try: You cannot crack the same one twice in a row.
why.tryLine: You cannot crack the same one twice in a row.

why.headline: Why 'growing pains' at night?
why.summary: Aches after a day of use, often in the legs. Not bones stretching like elastic while you watch.
why.try: A rub and a stretch. Tell a grown-up if it is one-sided and fierce.
why.tryLine: A rub and a stretch. Tell a grown-up if it is one-sided and fierce.

why.headline: Why a sore bump below the knee in sporty kids?
why.summary: A growth-plate tendon attachment gets overworked. Common. Named.
why.try: Rest beats heroics.
why.tryLine: Rest beats heroics.

why.headline: Why heels ache after new spikes?
why.summary: A growth area plus sudden load. The tendon shouts.
why.try: Two pairs of socks is not a personality. It is padding.
why.tryLine: Two pairs of socks is not a personality. It is padding.

why.headline: Why shins burn after a lot of pavement?
why.summary: Bone and the tissue on it get overloaded. The pain is a request, not a dare.
why.try: Softer ground. Fewer hero kilometres.
why.tryLine: Softer ground. Fewer hero kilometres.

why.headline: Why a bat or rope gives palm blisters fast?
why.summary: New rub on thin skin. The cushion bubble arrives overnight.
why.try: Tape before the second session.
why.tryLine: Tape before the second session.

why.headline: Why do pool eyes go red?
why.summary: Chlorine and other bits irritate the surface. Goggles are a porthole.
why.try: Rinse with fresh water after.
why.tryLine: Rinse with fresh water after.

why.headline: Why can blond hair go green in a pool?
why.summary: Copper in the water sticks to hair. Not the chlorine painting it.
why.try: A proper wash beats lemon folklore.
why.tryLine: A proper wash beats lemon folklore.

why.headline: Why do fingers wrinkle in a bath on purpose?
why.summary: Nerves trigger the wrinkle. The tread may help grip wet things. It is not just soggy skin.
why.try: Compare a gloved hand. That one stays smooth.
why.tryLine: Compare a gloved hand. That one stays smooth.

why.headline: Why does it take minutes to prune?
why.summary: The signal and the fluid shift are slow. Instant prune would be a magic trick.
why.try: Time it. Science likes a clock.
why.tryLine: Time it. Science likes a clock.

why.headline: Why does soap make hands slippery then squeaky?
why.summary: First it lifts oil. Then the oil is gone and skin-on-skin drags. Squeaky is clean, not damaged.
why.try: Rinse. The squeak is the end of the job.
why.tryLine: Rinse. The squeak is the end of the job.

why.headline: Why does tap water feel 'hard' in some towns?
why.summary: Extra minerals. Soap struggles. Kettles grow scale.
why.try: The scum is minerals plus soap, not dirt you missed.
why.tryLine: The scum is minerals plus soap, not dirt you missed.

why.headline: Why does soft water make more bubbles?
why.summary: Fewer minerals fight the soap. Suds go wild.
why.try: Same soap, different town, different foam.
why.tryLine: Same soap, different town, different foam.

why.headline: Why a white crust in the kettle?
why.summary: Hard-water minerals fall out when water boils. The crust is leftover rock.
why.try: Vinegar dissolves the rock. That is a grown-up job.
why.tryLine: Vinegar dissolves the rock. That is a grown-up job.

why.headline: Why a bike rusts after rain?
why.summary: Iron plus water plus air. The orange flake is iron giving up.
why.try: A wipe after rain is cheaper than a new chain.
why.tryLine: A wipe after rain is cheaper than a new chain.

why.headline: Why don't stainless pans rust like nails?
why.summary: Extra metals in the mix make a thin shield. 'Stainless' means stubborn, not immortal.
why.try: Salt and damage can still win.
why.tryLine: Salt and damage can still win.

why.headline: Why do copper coins go green?
why.summary: A copper-and-air crust. The green is a new compound, not mould.
why.try: The statue of liberty wears the same coat.
why.tryLine: The statue of liberty wears the same coat.

why.headline: Why silver jewellery goes dark?
why.summary: Sulphur in air makes a dark skin. A polish lifts it.
why.try: A felt bag slows the skin.
why.tryLine: A felt bag slows the skin.

why.headline: Why gold stays shiny?
why.summary: Gold barely reacts with air. That is why old coins still look rich.
why.try: It is lazy chemistry, not magic.
why.tryLine: It is lazy chemistry, not magic.

why.headline: Why is diamond so hard?
why.summary: Each carbon atom locks to four others in a tight 3D net. The net does not want to break.
why.try: Hard is not the same as unbreakable by a smash.
why.tryLine: Hard is not the same as unbreakable by a smash.

why.headline: Why is pencil 'lead' so soft?
why.summary: Also carbon, but in slippery sheets. The sheets slide onto the page.
why.try: Diamond and pencil are cousins with different furniture.
why.tryLine: Diamond and pencil are cousins with different furniture.

why.headline: Why does a rubber lift pencil?
why.summary: It grabs the graphite crumbs better than paper does and rolls them up.
why.try: A dirty rubber just paints the crumbs around.
why.tryLine: A dirty rubber just paints the crumbs around.

why.headline: Why some pens will not wash out?
why.summary: The dye binds or hides in the fibre. Water is not invited.
why.try: That is a feature until it is your shirt.
why.tryLine: That is a feature until it is your shirt.

why.headline: Why whiteboard ink wipes and permanent does not?
why.summary: Whiteboard ink sits on a slick film. Permanent soaks or sticks.
why.try: The wrong pen on a board is a sad afternoon.
why.tryLine: The wrong pen on a board is a sad afternoon.

why.headline: Why highlighters look lit from inside?
why.summary: They use fluorescent dye. Invisible UV turns into extra visible glow.
why.try: In sun they look even louder.
why.tryLine: In sun they look even louder.

why.headline: Why do plastic stars glow after lights-out?
why.summary: They store light energy and leak it slowly. Not nuclear. A slow battery of photons.
why.try: Charge them under a lamp. Darkness is the show.
why.tryLine: Charge them under a lamp. Darkness is the show.

why.headline: Why a blacklight makes white socks blaze?
why.summary: Whitening chemicals fluoresce. The purple lamp is the trigger.
why.try: Tonic water can glow too. Weird party trick.
why.tryLine: Tonic water can glow too. Weird party trick.

why.headline: Why a laser makes a tiny dot, not a flood?
why.summary: The beam is one colour, in step, and tight. Lenses keep it from spreading much.
why.try: Never at eyes. Tight also means punchy.
why.tryLine: Never at eyes. Tight also means punchy.

why.headline: Why a CD makes rainbows?
why.summary: Tiny tracks act like a grating. They split white light by colour.
why.try: Tilt it. The rainbow moves with the angle.
why.tryLine: Tilt it. The rainbow moves with the angle.

why.headline: Why an oil puddle is rainbow too?
why.summary: A thin film. Light bouncing from the top and bottom interferes. Colours cancel or add.
why.try: The thinnest film makes the loudest colours.
why.tryLine: The thinnest film makes the loudest colours.

why.headline: Why soap bubbles have swirling colour?
why.summary: Same thin-film trick as oil. As the wall thins, the colours shift.
why.try: Black patches mean the wall is about to pop.
why.tryLine: Black patches mean the wall is about to pop.

why.headline: Why a bubble pops when you touch it?
why.summary: Oil from skin wrecks the thin wall. A dry poke can be kinder than a wet one.
why.try: Gloves pop fewer, not zero.
why.tryLine: Gloves pop fewer, not zero.

why.headline: Why does helium go up?
why.summary: Helium atoms are lighter than the nitrogen-oxygen mix we call air. Gravity pulls air down harder.
why.try: A helium balloon is a bubble of 'less pull'.
why.tryLine: A helium balloon is a bubble of 'less pull'.

why.headline: Why a balloon looks sad in the cold?
why.summary: Cold air inside takes less space. The rubber follows.
why.try: Bring it in. It puffs without a pump.
why.tryLine: Bring it in. It puffs without a pump.

why.headline: Why party balloons droop overnight?
why.summary: Gas leaks through the rubber. Helium leaks faster. Morning is the audit.
why.try: Foil ones leak slower.
why.tryLine: Foil ones leak slower.

why.headline: Why a shock from a car door in winter?
why.summary: Dry air. Shoes scrape up charge. The metal is the exit.
why.try: Touch metal with a key first. The zap moves.
why.tryLine: Touch metal with a key first. The zap moves.

why.headline: Why thunder rumbles after a flash?
why.summary: Light wins. Sound jogs. The rumble is the long path and echoes.
why.try: Seconds / 3 ≈ kilometres.
why.tryLine: Seconds / 3 ≈ kilometres.

why.headline: Why close thunder cracks and far thunder growls?
why.summary: Near: one hard slap. Far: the slap is stretched and bounced.
why.try: The growl is distance, not a different storm.
why.tryLine: The growl is distance, not a different storm.

why.headline: Why rain on hot pavement smells like that?
why.summary: Oil and a soil chemical lift into the air. The nose has a name for it: petrichor.
why.try: The first drops smell strongest.
why.tryLine: The first drops smell strongest.

why.headline: Why a wet dog stinks more?
why.summary: Water wakes skin oils and bacteria. The shake shares them with the room.
why.try: A towel is diplomacy.
why.tryLine: A towel is diplomacy.

why.headline: Why a litter box announces itself?
why.summary: Ammonia from wee plus bacteria. Closed rooms concentrate the news.
why.try: Scooping is the whole product.
why.tryLine: Scooping is the whole product.

why.headline: Why a neglected tank smells swampy?
why.summary: Waste plus bacteria plus low oxygen. The swamp is a chemistry report.
why.try: A water change is the reset.
why.tryLine: A water change is the reset.

why.headline: Why ponds go green in summer?
why.summary: Warmth plus nutrients. Tiny plants bloom. The green is a crowd.
why.try: A stick swirl shows how thick the crowd is.
why.tryLine: A stick swirl shows how thick the crowd is.

why.headline: Why rocks in a stream are slippery?
why.summary: A film of algae. The slime is life, not washing-up liquid.
why.try: Step on dry stone. Pride is less important.
why.tryLine: Step on dry stone. Pride is less important.

why.headline: Why people say moss grows on the north side?
why.summary: In some places north is damper and shadier. Moss likes that. It is a clue, not a compass law.
why.try: Check all sides. Moss cheats.
why.tryLine: Check all sides. Moss cheats.

why.headline: Why a stump shows rings?
why.summary: Each year a new wood layer. Fat rings are easy years. Thin rings are hard ones.
why.try: Count from the edge in. That is age.
why.tryLine: Count from the edge in. That is age.

why.headline: Why a knot in a plank?
why.summary: A branch was there. The trunk buried it. The swirl is the branch's ghost.
why.try: Sanding will not erase a ghost.
why.tryLine: Sanding will not erase a ghost.

why.headline: Why trees bleed sticky sap?
why.summary: It is the tree's blood-and-bandage. Cuts leak it, then it seals.
why.try: It is not syrup until a person cooks maple.
why.tryLine: It is not syrup until a person cooks maple.

why.headline: Why pine sap smells like Christmas?
why.summary: The tree makes fragrant resins as a pest shield. We stole the smell for December.
why.try: A warm day makes the smell louder.
why.tryLine: A warm day makes the smell louder.

why.headline: Why pine cones open in the dry?
why.summary: Dry scales bend open and drop seeds. Wet weather shuts them to wait.
why.try: A damp cone on a radiator is a slow film.
why.tryLine: A damp cone on a radiator is a slow film.

why.headline: Why sycamore seeds spin?
why.summary: A wing makes them autorotate. They stay up longer and ride farther.
why.try: Drop two. The spinner beats the lump.
why.tryLine: Drop two. The spinner beats the lump.

why.headline: Why a dandelion becomes a white ball?
why.summary: Each seed grows a parachute. The ball is a launch pad.
why.try: One puff is a hundred tiny bets.
why.tryLine: One puff is a hundred tiny bets.

why.headline: Why burrs stick to dogs?
why.summary: Hooks. They hitch a ride to a new field. Velcro is a copy of this idea.
why.try: Pick them off outside. The carpet is not a field.
why.tryLine: Pick them off outside. The carpet is not a field.

why.headline: Why nettles sting?
why.summary: Hollow hairs inject a cocktail. The burn is chemistry, not a bite.
why.try: Dock leaves are folklore. Time is the real cure.
why.tryLine: Dock leaves are folklore. Time is the real cure.

why.headline: Why some plants give a rash days later?
why.summary: An oil on the leaf trains the immune system to overreact next time.
why.try: Do not burn the plant. The smoke carries the oil.
why.tryLine: Do not burn the plant. The smoke carries the oil.

why.headline: Why spring makes some people sneeze?
why.summary: Pollen is a protein dust. The immune system treats it like a threat. Histamine does the rest.
why.try: The sneeze is the overreaction, not the plant attacking.
why.tryLine: The sneeze is the overreaction, not the plant attacking.

why.headline: Why hay fever itches the eyes too?
why.summary: The same histamine hits eye tissues. Tears try to wash the dust.
why.try: Rubbing makes more histamine. Unfair but true.
why.tryLine: Rubbing makes more histamine. Unfair but true.

why.headline: Why a bee sting keeps hurting?
why.summary: The barb can stay and pump. Venom tells pain nerves to shout.
why.try: A grown-up scrapes, not squeezes.
why.tryLine: A grown-up scrapes, not squeezes.

why.headline: Why wasps can sting more than once?
why.summary: Their sting is a smooth needle. No barb to lose. They can reuse it.
why.try: Give them the jam. Walk.
why.tryLine: Give them the jam. Walk.

why.headline: Why some ants burn?
why.summary: Formic acid. The name even means ant.
why.try: A tiny red bump is the autograph.
why.tryLine: A tiny red bump is the autograph.

why.headline: Why a mosquito bite itches later?
why.summary: Their spit stops your blood clotting. Your immune system throws a party at the spit.
why.try: The itch is you, not the mosquito still there.
why.tryLine: The itch is you, not the mosquito still there.

why.headline: Why mosquitoes pick some people more?
why.summary: Breath carbon dioxide, heat, and skin chemicals. Some bodies are louder beacons.
