why.try: It is not 'sweet blood' folklore. It is chemistry.
why.tryLine: It is not 'sweet blood' folklore. It is chemistry.

why.headline: Why ticks hang on?
why.summary: They glue and drill for a long drink. The barbs face backward.
why.try: A proper pull. No burning folklore.
why.tryLine: A proper pull. No burning folklore.

why.headline: Why fleas jump so far?
why.summary: A spring protein stores energy and dumps it at once. For their size, they are rockets.
why.try: A pet is a better host than a human usually.
why.tryLine: A pet is a better host than a human usually.

why.headline: Why a web sticks to a fly but not the spider?
why.summary: Not every thread is glue. Spiders walk the dry ones. Flies hit the sticky ones.
why.try: A dew morning shows the whole map.
why.tryLine: A dew morning shows the whole map.

why.headline: Why a spider is not an insect?
why.summary: Eight legs. Two body parts. No wings. Insects signed a different contract.
why.try: Count legs before you name it.
why.tryLine: Count legs before you name it.

why.headline: Why snails leave silver?
why.summary: The slime is a road they build as they go. It cuts friction and stops them drying.
why.try: The silver is dried road.
why.tryLine: The silver is dried road.

why.headline: Why salt kills slugs — and why not to?
why.summary: Salt sucks water out. It is a cruel trick. A garden can do better.
why.try: Leave the salt in the kitchen.
why.tryLine: Leave the salt in the kitchen.

why.headline: Why worms come up in rain?
why.summary: Flooded soil is low oxygen. The surface is a gasp of air.
why.try: Puddles are worm traffic jams.
why.tryLine: Puddles are worm traffic jams.

why.headline: Why a chopped worm seems to become two?
why.summary: Only some pieces can regrow, and not into two happy worms like a cartoon.
why.try: Leave worms in one piece. They have enough problems.
why.tryLine: Leave worms in one piece. They have enough problems.

why.headline: Why so many legs?
why.summary: Each body segment brings a pair. More segments, more legs. The wave is how they walk.
why.try: Watch the wave, not each foot.
why.tryLine: Watch the wave, not each foot.

why.headline: Why millipedes curl into a spiral?
why.summary: Armour on the outside. Soft bits inside. A spiral is a shield.
why.try: Do not uncurl them for fun.
why.tryLine: Do not uncurl them for fun.

why.headline: Why woodlice live under pots?
why.summary: They are crustaceans that came ashore. They still need damp.
why.try: A dry path is a desert to them.
why.tryLine: A dry path is a desert to them.

why.headline: Why some woodlice roll into a ball?
why.summary: The same idea as an armadillo, pocket size.
why.try: A tap and they become a bead.
why.tryLine: A tap and they become a bead.

why.headline: Why moths spiral at a bulb?
why.summary: They steer by distant light like the moon. A bulb is a moon that keeps moving around them.
why.try: A porch light is a maze they did not ask for.
why.tryLine: A porch light is a maze they did not ask for.

why.headline: Why moths leave dust on your fingers?
why.summary: The dust is scales. They fly worse without them.
why.try: Look, don't rub.
why.tryLine: Look, don't rub.

why.headline: Why a butterfly tongue is a coil?
why.summary: It unrolls into a nectar straw. The coil is storage.
why.try: Watch one at a flower. The straw appears.
why.tryLine: Watch one at a flower. The straw appears.

why.headline: Why caterpillars do almost nothing but eat?
why.summary: They are a stomach with legs. The energy becomes a butterfly later.
why.try: The mess on the leaf is the bill.
why.tryLine: The mess on the leaf is the bill.

why.headline: Why a chrysalis looks still but is not?
why.summary: Inside, the body is being rebuilt. Still is not paused.
why.try: Do not 'help' it out. The struggle is part of the build.
why.tryLine: Do not 'help' it out. The struggle is part of the build.

why.headline: Why ladybirds have spots?
why.summary: A warning coat. Birds remember the nasty taste that came with the pattern.
why.try: Spot counts do not tell the age. That myth can retire.
why.tryLine: Spot counts do not tell the age. That myth can retire.

why.headline: Why some fireflies flash together?
why.summary: They lock onto neighbours. A field becomes a metronome.
why.try: A dark hill in the right country is the show.
why.tryLine: A dark hill in the right country is the show.

why.headline: Why crickets get louder at night?
why.summary: Males call for mates. Night is cooler and safer for a concert.
why.try: The tempo tracks the temperature.
why.tryLine: The tempo tracks the temperature.

why.headline: Why cicadas scream in summer trees?
why.summary: A drum-skin in the body. Males again. The tree is an amplifier.
why.try: Ear-level cicadas are a design flaw in the universe.
why.tryLine: Ear-level cicadas are a design flaw in the universe.

why.headline: Why ponds shout after dark?
why.summary: Frogs call when they are less likely to be lunch. Water carries the song.
why.try: Each species has a ringtone.
why.tryLine: Each species has a ringtone.

why.headline: Why people say toads give you warts?
why.summary: They do not. Human warts are a virus. Toads have bumps that look similar.
why.try: Wash hands anyway. Mud is still mud.
why.tryLine: Wash hands anyway. Mud is still mud.

why.headline: Why newts have flat tails?
why.summary: A paddle. Water is their other country.
why.try: Look for them in still ponds, not fast streams.
why.tryLine: Look for them in still ponds, not fast streams.

why.headline: Why the 'three-second goldfish' story is wrong?
why.summary: They can learn maps and times. The myth is lazy.
why.try: Feed at a regular hour. They will wait at the glass.
why.tryLine: Feed at a regular hour. They will wait at the glass.

why.headline: Why a fish sometimes looks like it yawns?
why.summary: It is often a gill stretch or a threat. Not boredom like ours.
why.try: Do not invent a tiny sofa.
why.tryLine: Do not invent a tiny sofa.

why.headline: Why sharks swing their heads?
why.summary: Nostrils sample left and right. The swing is a smell stereo.
why.try: They are following a trail, not nodding hello.
why.tryLine: They are following a trail, not nodding hello.

why.headline: Why rays hide under sand?
why.summary: Ambush plus camouflage. The sand is a blanket.
why.try: Shuffle feet in shallow water. That is the polite knock.
why.tryLine: Shuffle feet in shallow water. That is the polite knock.

why.headline: Why a starfish can grow an arm back?
why.summary: They are built to lose a limb to a predator and continue. Slow, but real.
why.try: Do not test this. The sea already does.
why.tryLine: Do not test this. The sea already does.

why.headline: Why sea anemones sting but clownfish do not care?
why.summary: A mucus coat. The fish is wearing a password.
why.try: The password is earned, not given to fingers.
why.tryLine: The password is earned, not given to fingers.

why.headline: Why coral looks like a plant but is an animal?
why.summary: Tiny animals in a limestone apartment, plus algae roommates. The colour is often the roommates.
why.try: Hot water evicts the roommates. That is bleaching.
why.tryLine: Hot water evicts the roommates. That is bleaching.

why.headline: Why tide pools are like tiny planets?
why.summary: Each is a world that resets twice a day. Heat, salt, and hunters change by the hour.
why.try: Look, don't stir. You are a giant in that world.
why.tryLine: Look, don't stir. You are a giant in that world.

why.headline: Why some seaweed has poppable bladders?
why.summary: Air floats the fronds toward light. The pop is you breaking a float.
why.try: One pop is curiosity. A massacre is just noise.
why.tryLine: One pop is curiosity. A massacre is just noise.

why.headline: Why driftwood looks bone-smooth?
why.summary: Salt, sun, and a million knocks sand it. Time is the sandpaper.
why.try: The grey is weathered lignin, not paint.
why.tryLine: The grey is weathered lignin, not paint.

why.headline: Why beach pebbles are round?
why.summary: They hit each other for years. Corners lose.
why.try: A sharp pebble is a newcomer.
why.tryLine: A sharp pebble is a newcomer.

why.headline: Why some sand squeaks?
why.summary: Dry grains rub in a certain size. The squeak is a chorus of collisions.
why.try: Wet sand goes quiet.
why.tryLine: Wet sand goes quiet.

why.headline: Why quicksand swallows slowly, not like a film?
why.summary: Saturated sand acts like a thick fluid. You sink, then it packs. Thrashing makes it worse.
why.try: Lean back. More surface, less sink.
why.tryLine: Lean back. More surface, less sink.

why.headline: Why dried mud makes polygons?
why.summary: As it shrinks, cracks meet at comfortable angles. The pattern is stress taking a holiday.
why.try: A puddle in a week is a map.
why.tryLine: A puddle in a week is a map.

why.headline: Why a tiny river can cut a huge canyon?
why.summary: Time plus sediment as sandpaper. Soft rock loses. Hard rock becomes walls.
why.try: The river is old. The drama is slow.
why.tryLine: The river is old. The drama is slow.

why.headline: Why waterfalls move upstream over ages?
why.summary: The lip wears. The fall takes a step back. Niagara is walking, very slowly.
why.try: A photo from a century ago is the proof.
why.tryLine: A photo from a century ago is the proof.

why.headline: Why limestone country is full of caves?
why.summary: Slightly acid water dissolves the rock along cracks. A drip becomes a hall.
why.try: Helmets exist for a reason.
why.tryLine: Helmets exist for a reason.

why.headline: Why icicle-rocks hang from cave roofs?
why.summary: Drips leave a little mineral each time. Hang = stalactite. Floor pile = stalagmite.
why.try: They grow like fingernails of stone.
why.tryLine: They grow like fingernails of stone.

why.headline: Why caves echo more than bedrooms?
why.summary: Hard wet walls, big empty volume. Sound takes the scenic route back.
why.try: A shout is a tape measure.
why.tryLine: A shout is a tape measure.

why.headline: Why a whisper can travel a curved wall?
why.summary: The curve keeps the sound hugging the surface. A shortcut for a secret.
why.try: Cathedrals love this trick.
why.tryLine: Cathedrals love this trick.

why.headline: Why a bell can be heard across a town?
why.summary: A big metal shape rings at a pitch the air carries well. Height helps it clear roofs.
why.try: Listen for the second, softer hit — that's the town answering.
why.tryLine: Listen for the second, softer hit — that's the town answering.

why.headline: Why foghorns are so low?
why.summary: Low notes travel farther in thick air and around obstacles. A squeak would die at the pier.
why.try: The gloom is why they exist.
why.tryLine: The gloom is why they exist.

why.headline: Why a lighthouse blinks a pattern?
why.summary: Each tower has a signature so sailors know which rock they nearly found.
why.try: A chart is the decoder ring.
why.tryLine: A chart is the decoder ring.

why.headline: Why port is red and starboard green?
why.summary: A rule so two boats can tell who should give way at night. Left/right painted on the world.
why.try: Face the bow. Red is left.
why.tryLine: Face the bow. Red is left.

why.headline: Why a sailboat has a deep fin?
why.summary: Wind wants to tip and shove sideways. The keel grabs water and argues back.
why.try: No keel, just a leaf.
why.tryLine: No keel, just a leaf.

why.headline: Why you can sail toward the wind, but not straight into it?
why.summary: The sail is a wing. It makes lift at an angle. Dead ahead there is no angle, only flap.
why.try: Zigzag is the path. It has a name: tacking.
why.tryLine: Zigzag is the path. It has a name: tacking.

why.headline: Why an anchor is not just a weight?
why.summary: The shape digs when the chain pulls flat. A brick would drag.
why.try: Scope — lots of chain — is the secret, not more iron.
why.tryLine: Scope — lots of chain — is the secret, not more iron.

why.headline: Why a lifejacket works even if you panic?
why.summary: Foam is less dense than water. It holds the mouth up. Skill is optional; buoyancy is not.
why.try: Try one in a pool with a grown-up. The lift is rude and kind.
why.tryLine: Try one in a pool with a grown-up. The lift is rude and kind.

why.headline: Why we only see the tip of an iceberg?
why.summary: Ice is a bit less dense than seawater. Most of the berg hides to stay in balance.
why.try: Nine-tenths is the cliché because it is roughly true.
why.tryLine: Nine-tenths is the cliché because it is roughly true.

why.headline: Why thick lake ice can hold a truck?
why.summary: A sheet spreads the load. Thickness plus cold is a bridge. Thin ice is a lie.
why.try: If you cannot see how thick, you do not walk.
why.tryLine: If you cannot see how thick, you do not walk.

why.headline: Why black ice is invisible?
why.summary: A thin clear glaze on dark tarmac. You see the road, not the trap.
why.try: A shine that should not be there is the tell.
why.tryLine: A shine that should not be there is the tell.

why.headline: Why windows grow ferns of frost?
why.summary: Ice crystals copy tiny scratches and dust. The fern is a family tree of cold.
why.try: A morning pane is a gallery.
why.tryLine: A morning pane is a gallery.

why.headline: Why trees go white overnight without snow?
why.summary: Water vapour turns straight to ice on cold twigs. No cloud required.
why.try: It looks like sugar. It is weather.
why.tryLine: It looks like sugar. It is weather.

why.headline: Why mountain posts wear icy fur?
why.summary: Supercooled fog freezes on the windward side. The fur points at the weather.
why.try: The hairy side is the wind's signature.
why.tryLine: The hairy side is the wind's signature.

why.headline: Why icicles have rings?
why.summary: Melt by day, freeze by night. Each night adds a sleeve.
why.try: A warm noon is when they drip their biography.
why.tryLine: A warm noon is when they drip their biography.

why.headline: Why no two snowflakes match?
why.summary: Each takes a different path through changing air. The arms record the trip.
why.try: The six-fold bit is the rule. The details are the diary.
why.tryLine: The six-fold bit is the rule. The details are the diary.

why.headline: Why snowflakes have six arms?
why.summary: Water molecules lock at 120-degree angles. Six is the geometry, not a committee vote.
why.try: Look close. The rule holds even when arms break.
why.tryLine: Look close. The rule holds even when arms break.

why.headline: Why wet snow packs and powder does not?
why.summary: A little melt-water is glue. Deep-cold powder is just dry crystals.
why.try: The perfect ball is a temperature, not a talent.
why.tryLine: The perfect ball is a temperature, not a talent.

why.headline: Why very cold snow squeaks?
why.summary: Crystals grind instead of smear. The squeak is winter percussion.
why.try: Warmer snow just crumps.
why.tryLine: Warmer snow just crumps.

why.headline: Why you do not eat yellow snow?
why.summary: It is usually wee. The joke is a warning.
why.try: White only. Even then, cities are not kitchens.
why.tryLine: White only. Even then, cities are not kitchens.

why.headline: Why a slope can let go all at once?
why.summary: A weak layer fails. The slab above becomes a sliding plate.
why.try: A bang and a whoomph are the mountain talking. Leave.
why.tryLine: A bang and a whoomph are the mountain talking. Leave.

why.headline: Why a glacier moves if it is solid?
why.summary: Ice flows, slowly, under its own weight. A river that forgot to be liquid.
why.try: The cracks are crevasses — doors into the flow.
why.tryLine: The cracks are crevasses — doors into the flow.

why.headline: Why dirty stripes sit on glaciers?
why.summary: Rock the ice picked up and dumped. The stripe is a conveyor belt's trash.
why.try: The end pile is a moraine. A hill with a past.
why.tryLine: The end pile is a moraine. A hill with a past.

why.headline: Why a huge boulder sits in a field alone?
why.summary: Ice carried it and melted. The boulder is a hitchhiker that missed the last ride.
why.try: It will not match the local bedrock. That is the clue.
why.tryLine: It will not match the local bedrock. That is the clue.

why.headline: Why seashells sit on mountain rocks?
why.summary: The rock used to be a seabed. Continents shoved it up. The shells did not hike.
why.try: A hill can be an old ocean.
why.tryLine: A hill can be an old ocean.

why.headline: Why some fossils look like ram horns?
why.summary: Ammonites built spiral homes. Stone filled the rooms.
why.try: The spiral is a staircase of chambers.
why.tryLine: The spiral is a staircase of chambers.

why.headline: Why scientists say birds are dinosaurs?
why.summary: The bones, hips, and feathers line up. Some dinos already had wings in the family.
why.try: A chicken is a punchline and a fact.
why.tryLine: A chicken is a punchline and a fact.

why.headline: Why feathers beat fur for flight?
why.summary: Light, stiff, and they make an airfoil. Fur cannot be a wing.
why.try: Stroke a flight feather. The vane zips back together.
why.tryLine: Stroke a flight feather. The vane zips back together.

why.headline: Why birds nibble their own feathers?
why.summary: They zip vanes and spread oil. A messy bird is a cold bird.
why.try: The 'itch' is maintenance.
why.tryLine: The 'itch' is maintenance.

why.headline: Why birds stand on one leg?
why.summary: They tuck the other to save heat. A flamingo is not showing off. It is thrifty.
why.try: Watch which leg they swap.
why.tryLine: Watch which leg they swap.

why.headline: Why a pigeon's head jabs when it walks?
why.summary: The head parks to get a clear picture, then catches up. The jab is a camera gimbal.
why.try: Film it and pause. The head is the still bit.
why.tryLine: Film it and pause. The head is the still bit.

why.headline: Why owls can twist so far?
why.summary: Extra neck bones and loose arteries. They compensate for eyes that cannot roll.
why.try: Do not copy. Your neck signed a different contract.
why.tryLine: Do not copy. Your neck signed a different contract.

why.headline: Why owl eyes look huge?
why.summary: Night tubes. They gather scraps of light. The face is a dish for sound too.
why.try: A barn at dusk is their cinema.
why.tryLine: A barn at dusk is their cinema.

why.headline: Why some bat calls are silent to us?
why.summary: Too high. Kids hear higher than grown-ups. Bats go higher still.
why.try: A detector turns their shout into our beep.
why.tryLine: A detector turns their shout into our beep.

why.headline: Why bats eat so many insects?
why.summary: Night shift, wide mouth, echolocation. A hungry bat is a flying sieve.
why.try: A porch light is a bat buffet.
why.tryLine: A porch light is a bat buffet.

why.headline: Why a hedgehog becomes a spike ball?
why.summary: A muscle pulls the coat into a sphere. The face hides.
why.try: Leave it. Unrolling is their job.
why.tryLine: Leave it. Unrolling is their job.

why.headline: Why a fox can sound like a person at night?
why.summary: A mating call that uses a raw throat. The shock is the point.
why.try: A January night is their opera.
why.tryLine: A January night is their opera.

why.headline: Why badgers have doorways in woods?
why.summary: A sett is a family tunnel system used for decades. The dirt fan is the welcome mat.
why.try: Do not block a hole. Someone lives there.
why.tryLine: Do not block a hole. Someone lives there.

why.headline: Why lawns get volcanoes of dirt?
why.summary: A mole is mining worms. The hill is the spoil heap.
why.try: The lawn is a larder from below.
why.tryLine: The lawn is a larder from below.

why.headline: Why squirrels bury nuts and forget some?
why.summary: They remember many. The forgotten ones become trees. Forgetfulness plants forests.
why.try: A winter lawn with holes is a pantry.
why.tryLine: A winter lawn with holes is a pantry.

why.headline: Why a squirrel runs a crazy path from a dog?
why.summary: Unpredictable prey is hard to catch. The zigzag is a strategy.
why.try: The dog is not invited to understand.
why.tryLine: The dog is not invited to understand.

why.headline: Why rabbits thump?
why.summary: An alarm drum. The ground carries it to the warren.
why.try: A field of still ears after a thump is the meeting.
why.tryLine: A field of still ears after a thump is the meeting.

why.headline: Why rabbit teeth never stop growing?
why.summary: They wear them down on plants. Growth matches the grind.
why.try: Cardboard is a dentist, not a toy, for pets.
why.tryLine: Cardboard is a dentist, not a toy, for pets.

why.headline: Why horses can doze standing?
why.summary: A stay apparatus locks the legs. Deep sleep still needs a lie-down.
why.try: A horse that never lies down is a tired horse.
why.tryLine: A horse that never lies down is a tired horse.

why.headline: Why horse ears swivel like radar?
why.summary: Each ear aims at a different sound. The face tells you the attention map.
why.try: Angry ears go back. That is the whole email.
why.tryLine: Angry ears go back. That is the whole email.

why.headline: Why cows look like they chew gum for hours?
why.summary: They ferment grass in extra stomachs, then rechew it. Cud is the second sitting.
why.try: A field of sideways jaws is a factory.
why.tryLine: A field of sideways jaws is a factory.

why.headline: Why a sitting cow can mean rain in folklore?
why.summary: Sometimes they rest more in humid air. Sometimes they just sit. Folklore loves a pattern.
why.try: Check the sky anyway.
why.tryLine: Check the sky anyway.

why.headline: Why sheep copy the one in front?
why.summary: Safety in a moving clump. The flock is the plan.
why.try: A sheepdog is a living fence.
why.tryLine: A sheepdog is a living fence.

why.headline: Why goats stand on cliffs like they have glue?
why.summary: Hooves with a hard edge and a rubbery pad. Plus a brain that likes a view.
why.try: A barn roof is, to a goat, a suggestion.
why.tryLine: A barn roof is, to a goat, a suggestion.

why.headline: Why pigs wallow?
why.summary: They cannot sweat much. Mud is sunscreen and air-con.
why.try: Clean pigs in hot sun are uncomfortable pigs.
why.tryLine: Clean pigs in hot sun are uncomfortable pigs.

why.headline: Why chickens take dust baths?
why.summary: Dust wrecks parasites. The 'bath' is a dry shower.
why.try: A bald patch of yard is the spa.
why.tryLine: A bald patch of yard is the spa.

why.headline: Why roosters shout before you wanted to wake?
why.summary: They claim the morning. Light plus habit. The clock is in their head.
why.try: Earplugs are older than cities.
why.tryLine: Earplugs are older than cities.

why.headline: Why a hen sits so long?
why.summary: Heat runs the embryo's clock. Leave, and the clock stutters.
why.try: Twenty-one days is the chicken contract.
why.tryLine: Twenty-one days is the chicken contract.

why.headline: Why a chick has a tiny horn on its beak?
why.summary: An egg tooth. It zips the shell. Then it falls off.
why.try: Do not 'help' a hatch. The zip is exercise.
why.tryLine: Do not 'help' a hatch. The zip is exercise.

why.headline: Why ducklings follow in a line?
why.summary: Imprinting. The first big moving thing is mum. The line is a rule they cannot unsee.
why.try: A person can accidentally become mum. Don't.
why.tryLine: A person can accidentally become mum. Don't.

why.headline: Why swans hiss?
why.summary: A warning with no teeth. The wings are the real threat.
why.try: Give them the path. Pride is not a lifejacket.
why.tryLine: Give them the path. Pride is not a lifejacket.

why.headline: Why a goose will chase you?
why.summary: Territory plus a neck that thinks it is a spear.
why.try: Do not run in a flap. Walk, side-on, leave.
why.tryLine: Do not run in a flap. Walk, side-on, leave.

why.headline: Why a peacock train is so extra?
why.summary: A billboard for health. The eyespots are a test the hens set.
why.try: The 'tail' is not the tail. True tail is the short bit that holds it.
why.tryLine: The 'tail' is not the tail. True tail is the short bit that holds it.

why.headline: Why crows sometimes leave shiny junk?
why.summary: Curious, social, and they notice people who feed them. A bottle cap is not rent. It is overlap.
why.try: Do not start a trash museum on purpose.
why.tryLine: Do not start a trash museum on purpose.

why.headline: Why crows can remember a mean face?
why.summary: They tell each other. A grudge can last years.
why.try: Be polite to the black birds. They have notes.
why.tryLine: Be polite to the black birds. They have notes.

why.headline: Why magpies shout from TV aerials?
why.summary: Sentinels. The shout is 'I see you' to the whole street.
why.try: A pair is a neighbourhood watch.
why.tryLine: A pair is a neighbourhood watch.

why.headline: Why robins look tame in winter?
why.summary: Hungry and used to gardeners turning soil. Bold is a strategy.
why.try: A worm is the whole conversation.
why.tryLine: A worm is the whole conversation.

why.headline: Why blue tits hang upside down on feeders?
why.summary: They forage that way in trees. The feeder is just another twig.
why.try: Watch the acrobatics. Gravity lost.
why.tryLine: Watch the acrobatics. Gravity lost.

why.headline: Why a dead tree is full of holes?
why.summary: Food plus future flats. A 'messy' tree is a block of flats.
why.try: Leave standing deadwood if it cannot crush a path.
why.tryLine: Leave standing deadwood if it cannot crush a path.

why.headline: Why an owl coughs up a furry lump?
why.summary: They swallow prey whole. Bones and fur come back as a pellet.
why.try: Unrolling one is a bone museum. Gloves.
why.tryLine: Unrolling one is a bone museum. Gloves.

why.headline: Why a kestrel can hang in the wind?
why.summary: It flies at the exact speed of the breeze. Stillness is motion in disguise.
why.try: A motorway verge is their restaurant.
why.tryLine: A motorway verge is their restaurant.

why.headline: Why gulls rob chips?
why.summary: They learned cities are cliffs with snacks. Bold birds get calories.
why.try: A stare-down is their opening move. Eat inside.
why.tryLine: A stare-down is their opening move. Eat inside.

why.headline: Why cities have so many pigeons?
why.summary: We replaced cliffs with ledges and wolves with crumbs. They said yes.
why.try: A flock lift-off is a grey weather system.
why.tryLine: A flock lift-off is a grey weather system.

why.headline: Why starlings make those huge night swirls?
why.summary: Each bird copies a few neighbours. The cloud is a maths trick with feathers.
why.try: A winter roost is the show. Stay till dusk.
why.tryLine: A winter roost is the show. Stay till dusk.

why.headline: Why swallows line up on wires?
why.summary: A pre-migration meeting. Bugs plus gossip.
why.try: August wires are a calendar.
why.tryLine: August wires are a calendar.

why.headline: Why swifts can stay airborne for months?
why.summary: They eat, drink, and even nap on the wing. Landing is optional.
why.try: A scream overhead in July is their name.
why.tryLine: A scream overhead in July is their name.

why.headline: Why a hummingbird can hover?
why.summary: Wings in a figure-eight. Lift on the way forward and back. A helicopter with nectar on its mind.
why.try: A red feeder is a trap they chose.
why.tryLine: A red feeder is a trap they chose.

why.headline: Why emperor penguins huddle and rotate?
why.summary: The middle is a radiator. The edge birds take turns in the freezer.
why.try: A huddle is a queue, not a cuddle.
why.tryLine: A huddle is a queue, not a cuddle.

why.headline: Why penguins toboggan on their bellies?
why.summary: Faster than walking, and it saves energy. Ice is a slide they grew up with.
why.try: The belly is a ski.
why.tryLine: The belly is a ski.

why.headline: Why some seals clap underwater?
why.summary: A display. Sound carries. The clap is a statement.
why.try: A head sticking up is only half the show.
why.tryLine: A head sticking up is only half the show.

why.headline: Why a whale blow looks like a fountain?
why.summary: Warm wet air hits cold. A cloud, plus leftover water in the nostril.
why.try: The shape of the spout can name the species.
why.tryLine: The shape of the spout can name the species.

why.headline: Why humpbacks sing for hours?
why.summary: Long patterned calls. Probably maps and mates. The ocean is their hall.
why.try: A hydrophone turns the hall into headphones.
why.tryLine: A hydrophone turns the hall into headphones.

why.headline: Why dolphins click at you?
why.summary: Echolocation. They are seeing your insides with sound.
why.try: A grin is their face, not always a mood.
why.tryLine: A grin is their face, not always a mood.

why.headline: Why an octopus arm can taste?
why.summary: Suckers have sensors. The arm decides before the head finishes the meeting.
why.try: A tank glass is a menu they can lick.
why.tryLine: A tank glass is a menu they can lick.

why.headline: Why octopuses squirt ink?
why.summary: A smoke bomb plus a taste that bothers noses. The blob can even look like a fake body.
why.try: The getaway is the point.
why.tryLine: The getaway is the point.

why.headline: Why cuttlefish change like a screen?
why.summary: Tiny colour bags and reflectors in the skin. The brain is a VJ.

why.summary: Pressure and friction make a whisper of water. The blade hydroplanes on a ghost.
why.try: A dull blade is just a metal foot.
why.tryLine: A dull blade is just a metal foot.

why.headline: Why curling teams sweep the ice?
why.summary: Sweeping warms and polishes. The stone travels farther on the ghost water.
why.try: The shouting is physics plus hope.
why.tryLine: The shouting is physics plus hope.

why.headline: Why rink ice is so white?
why.summary: They paint and flood in layers. White hides the concrete and shows the puck.
why.try: The shine is a thin last flood.
why.tryLine: The shine is a thin last flood.

why.headline: Why a puck slides so far?
why.summary: Vulcanised rubber plus that ghost water. Frozen rubber is a stone that changed its mind.
why.try: A warm puck would be a sad bun.
why.tryLine: A warm puck would be a sad bun.

why.headline: Why a goalie mask looks like a cartoon skull?
why.summary: It is a billboard and a shield. The paint is personality over armour.
why.try: The cage is the real face.
why.tryLine: The cage is the real face.

why.headline: Why offside exists in so many sports?
why.summary: To stop goal-hanging. A rule that makes the game a chase, not a camp.
why.try: The flag is a story about fairness.
why.tryLine: The flag is a story about fairness.

why.headline: Why a whistle can give a free shot?
why.summary: A foul near goal steals a chance. The penalty is the stolen chance, formalised.
why.try: The run-up is theatre. The kick is maths.
why.tryLine: The run-up is theatre. The kick is maths.

why.headline: Why a referee's whistle cuts through a crowd?
why.summary: A sharp high burst. Ears cannot ignore it. The pea inside makes the trill.
why.try: No pea, still loud. With pea, annoying on purpose.
why.tryLine: No pea, still loud. With pea, annoying on purpose.

why.headline: Why screens now argue with referees?
why.summary: Cameras catch angles a human in the middle cannot. The wait is the argument becoming a decision.
why.try: The groan is part of the new sport.
why.tryLine: The groan is part of the new sport.

why.headline: Why a race can end in a photograph?
why.summary: Bodies lean. Time is thinner than an eye. The strip camera is the judge.
why.try: A chest, not a nose, is often the rule.
why.tryLine: A chest, not a nose, is often the rule.

why.headline: Why sprinters use blocks?
why.summary: They let you push backward to go forward. The crouch is a coiled spring.
why.try: Standing starts waste the first bite.
why.tryLine: Standing starts waste the first bite.

why.headline: Why a twitch can kill a race?
why.summary: Leaving before the gun is a stolen millisecond. The rule is harsh because the edge is tiny.
why.try: The second gun is the sad one.
why.tryLine: The second gun is the sad one.

why.headline: Why relays drop the stick?
why.summary: A tiny object, tired hands, a moving target. The handoff is the whole sport in a second.
why.try: Practice the zone, not just the sprint.
why.tryLine: Practice the zone, not just the sprint.

why.headline: Why hurdlers do not jump, they run over?
why.summary: A jump would kill speed. The lead leg is a flick. The trail leg folds.
why.try: Watch the hips. They stay level-ish.
why.tryLine: Watch the hips. They stay level-ish.

why.headline: Why the landing is sand, not grass?
why.summary: Sand spreads the stop. Grass would be a bone meeting.
why.try: The rake is dignity for the next person.
why.tryLine: The rake is dignity for the next person.

why.headline: Why high jumpers go over backward?
why.summary: The Fosbury flop keeps the hips high and the head out of the way. A 1968 idea that ate the old style.
why.try: The mat is why the flop is legal.
why.tryLine: The mat is why the flop is legal.

why.headline: Why a bendy pole throws a person over a bar?
why.summary: The pole stores the run as spring, then gives it back upward. A catapult you hold.
why.try: The plant box is the hinge of the whole trick.
why.tryLine: The plant box is the hinge of the whole trick.

why.headline: Why a javelin is thrown at a slight angle?
why.summary: Too flat and it dives. Too steep and it stalls. The angle is a compromise with air.
why.try: The cord grip is for spin, not decoration.
why.tryLine: The cord grip is for spin, not decoration.

why.headline: Why discus throwers spin?
why.summary: The spin stores speed. The release is a sling.
why.try: A wild spin without a release is just dizziness.
why.tryLine: A wild spin without a release is just dizziness.

why.headline: Why a shot is a ball you shove, not throw?
why.summary: Rules. A throw with a straight arm is a different event. The shove keeps it ugly and fair.
why.try: The circle is a tiny country. Do not hop out.
why.tryLine: The circle is a tiny country. Do not hop out.

why.headline: Why that ball on a wire is called a hammer?
why.summary: Old field games used a sledgehammer. The name stayed; the tool got weirder.
why.try: The cage exists because physics is not polite.
why.tryLine: The cage exists because physics is not polite.

why.headline: Why a marathon is 42.195 km?
why.summary: A race plus a royal box in 1908, then the number froze. History, not a nice round science.
why.try: The extra metres are a king's fault.
why.tryLine: The extra metres are a king's fault.

why.headline: Why some people run farther than that on purpose?
why.summary: A different sport: fuel, feet, and stubbornness. The brain is the last muscle.
why.try: The medal is the least interesting part.
why.tryLine: The medal is the least interesting part.

why.headline: Why goggles make the pool clearer?
why.summary: They keep water off the eye so the surface stays a lens, not a sting.
why.try: A leak is a hair. Fix the seal, not your mood.
why.tryLine: A leak is a hair. Fix the seal, not your mood.

why.headline: Why those floating ropes?
why.summary: They kill waves between swimmers. The lane is a peace treaty.
why.try: The wave-eater discs are the whole point.
why.tryLine: The wave-eater discs are the whole point.

why.headline: Why a medley mixes four strokes?
why.summary: To test the awkward ones, not just the fast crawl. Fly first because it is the meanest when you are fresh.
why.try: Breaststroke after fly is a personality test.
why.tryLine: Breaststroke after fly is a personality test.

why.headline: Why a good dive whispers?
why.summary: Hands cut a hole. The body follows. A splash is knees inventing a door.
why.try: The rip entry is a hole, not a slap.
why.tryLine: The rip entry is a hole, not a slap.

why.headline: Why a cannonball is all splash?
why.summary: Maximum area hits at once. The crater is the joke.
why.try: Tuck tight. The joke has a technique.
why.tryLine: Tuck tight. The joke has a technique.

why.headline: Why lifeguards hate the biggest bombs?
why.summary: The wave hits little kids and the tiles. Fun has a radius.
why.try: Save the crater for the deep end.
why.tryLine: Save the crater for the deep end.

why.headline: Why lane one can feel slower?
why.summary: Waves bounce off the wall. Middle lanes are quieter water.
why.try: A home meet in lane four is a gift.
why.tryLine: A home meet in lane four is a gift.

why.headline: Why swimmers tumble at the wall?
why.summary: It is faster than touching and turning like a polite person. The push is the prize.
why.try: The flags tell you the wall is coming.
why.tryLine: The flags tell you the wall is coming.

why.headline: Why flags hang over backstrokers?
why.summary: They cannot see the wall. The flags are a countdown.
why.try: Five strokes after the flags is a common recipe.
why.tryLine: Five strokes after the flags is a common recipe.

why.headline: Why a twitch on the block is death?
why.summary: Same as track. The water remembers who jumped.
why.try: The recall is a rope or a second gun. Ugly either way.
why.tryLine: The recall is a rope or a second gun. Ugly either way.

why.headline: Why water polo hats have ear guards?
why.summary: Elbows and ball. The plastic is a helmet for the bits that stick out.
why.try: The number is a name you can read wet.
why.tryLine: The number is a name you can read wet.

why.headline: Why artistic swimmers smile upside down?
why.summary: It is scored. The smile is part of the apparatus. The lungs are the secret apparatus.
why.try: A nose clip is not a fashion.
why.tryLine: A nose clip is not a fashion.

why.headline: Why rowers slide on their seats?
why.summary: Legs are stronger than arms. The slide lets the legs do the expensive work.
why.try: Arms finish. Legs start. That order is religion.
why.tryLine: Arms finish. Legs start. That order is religion.

why.headline: Why a small person shouts in a racing boat?
why.summary: Steering plus timing plus weight we can spare. The voice is a metronome with opinions.
why.try: A good cox is worth more than a bigger engine.
why.tryLine: A good cox is worth more than a bigger engine.

why.headline: Why a kayak skirt?
why.summary: It keeps the river out of your lap. A wet lap is a slower boat.
why.try: The grab loop is how you leave in a hurry.
why.tryLine: The grab loop is how you leave in a hurry.

why.headline: Why canoeists often kneel?
why.summary: Lower, stabler, more power from the torso. A chair is a picnic, not a race.
why.try: The bruise on the shin is the receipt.
why.tryLine: The bruise on the shin is the receipt.

why.headline: Why a good paddle has a drip ring?
why.summary: So the river does not run down into your sleeve. Tiny plastic, huge mood.
why.try: Cold water in a cuff is a personality test.
why.tryLine: Cold water in a cuff is a personality test.

why.headline: Why they are ugly orange or lime?
why.summary: Searchers need a shout of colour in grey water. Taste lost. Visibility won.
why.try: Fashion is for dry land.
why.tryLine: Fashion is for dry land.

why.headline: Why a compass needle is a thin red friend?
why.summary: A magnet lined up with Earth's field. Red usually seeks north. Check your model.
why.try: Metal fence posts are rude to needles.
why.tryLine: Metal fence posts are rude to needles.

why.headline: Why wiggly brown lines mean hills?
why.summary: Each line is a height. Tight wiggles are steep. A circle is a summit or a hole — read the numbers.
why.try: A finger along a valley is how you do not climb by accident.
why.tryLine: A finger along a valley is how you do not climb by accident.

why.headline: Why maps have those letters and numbers?
why.summary: A box in a box. Along the corridor, up the stairs.
why.try: The joke is the whole method.
why.tryLine: The joke is the whole method.

why.headline: Why UK footpaths are dashed green or pink on maps?
why.summary: Rights of way painted so you can argue with a farmer using paper.
why.try: The dash is a legal spell.
why.tryLine: The dash is a legal spell.

why.headline: Why a fence has a tiny wooden staircase?
why.summary: People over, sheep not. A compromise in timber.
why.try: The dog latch is the other compromise.
why.tryLine: The dog latch is the other compromise.

why.headline: Why that swinging gate you have to hug?
why.summary: One person, no flock. The hug is the mechanism.
why.try: Do not fight it. It is smarter than a latch.
why.tryLine: Do not fight it. It is smarter than a latch.

why.headline: Why hikers stack stones on summits?
why.summary: A breadcrumb in fog. Also a bad habit when every tourist adds one.
why.try: A useful cairn is on a path. A new pile on a rare plant is vandalism.
why.tryLine: A useful cairn is on a path. A new pile on a rare plant is vandalism.

why.headline: Why trees get painted marks in woods?
why.summary: Trail waymarks. A language of dots and stripes.
why.try: Three in a triangle often means the path turns. Learn the local dialect.
why.tryLine: Three in a triangle often means the path turns. Learn the local dialect.

why.headline: Why mountain paths zigzag?
why.summary: A shallow slope you can walk all day beats a heroic scramble you regret.
why.try: The shortcut gully is how paths die.
why.tryLine: The shortcut gully is how paths die.

why.headline: Why that slope of loose stones feels alive?
why.summary: Each step is a small landslide. The mountain is moving house.
why.try: Traverse, do not ski it in trainers.
why.tryLine: Traverse, do not ski it in trainers.

why.headline: Why a ridge can feel like a roof?
why.summary: Two valleys carved either side. You are on the leftover.
why.try: Wind lives here. Hats do not.
why.tryLine: Wind lives here. Hats do not.

why.headline: Why walkers aim for the saddle, not the peak?
why.summary: The low point between tops is the door. Peaks are optional.
why.try: A col is a handshake between two hills.
why.tryLine: A col is a handshake between two hills.

why.headline: Why a concrete pillar on so many UK tops?
why.summary: Old mapping stations. A triangle network measured the country.
why.try: The plate on top is the business end.
why.tryLine: The plate on top is the business end.

why.headline: Why unlocked huts exist in wild hills?
why.summary: Shelter as a gift. You leave it better. That is the whole law.
why.try: A bothy book is the guest list of weather.
why.tryLine: A bothy book is the guest list of weather.

why.headline: Why a tiny tent is kinder than a big one?
why.summary: Less scar, less wind, less you. Dawn should hide the fact you were there.
why.try: Arrive late, leave early. The hill is not a festival.
why.tryLine: Arrive late, leave early. The hill is not a festival.

why.headline: Why a camping stove hates a breeze?
why.summary: Wind steals the flame's heat. A tiny shield is a three-course meal.
why.try: Kneel. You are the other shield.
why.tryLine: Kneel. You are the other shield.

why.headline: Why mountain streams can still make you ill?
why.summary: Sheep upstairs. Invisible guests. Clear is not clean.
why.try: A filter or a boil is the password.
why.tryLine: A filter or a boil is the password.

why.headline: Why old kits used iodine drops?
why.summary: A chemical bouncer for microbes. Taste is the tax.
why.try: Filters plus time beat nostalgia.
why.tryLine: Filters plus time beat nostalgia.

why.headline: Why map north and compass north disagree?
why.summary: The pole the needle wants is not the grid. The gap has a name and a number.
why.try: The margin of the map tells you the argument.
why.tryLine: The margin of the map tells you the argument.

why.headline: Why auroras like the poles?
why.summary: Earth's field funnels the solar wind there. The glow is the crash.
why.try: A dark, high, cold night is the ticket.
why.tryLine: A dark, high, cold night is the ticket.

why.headline: Why the Milky Way is a smear, not dots?
why.summary: Too many stars for the eye to split. The smear is our own galaxy edge-on.
why.try: A phone on a wall for 15 seconds cheats better than an eye.
why.tryLine: A phone on a wall for 15 seconds cheats better than an eye.

why.headline: Why a 'star' slides and then fades?
why.summary: A satellite catching sun. The fade is it slipping into Earth's shadow.
why.try: After twilight, the sky is a motorway.
why.tryLine: After twilight, the sky is a motorway.

why.headline: Why the Space Station can be brighter than jets?
why.summary: Huge, low, and it mirrors the sun. No blink, no sound.
why.try: A tracker app is a timetable for a moving room.
why.tryLine: A tracker app is a timetable for a moving room.

why.headline: Why some satellites used to flash like a camera?
why.summary: Flat antennas catching the sun. Many of those are gone. The memory remains.
why.try: A slow bright glide is still worth a shout.
why.tryLine: A slow bright glide is still worth a shout.

why.headline: Why some shooting stars look green?
why.summary: The metal in the grain burns with a colour. Green often means nickel or magnesium.
why.try: A shower night is a chemistry set.
why.tryLine: A shower night is a chemistry set.

why.headline: Why a meteor can boom?
why.summary: A bigger rock makes a shock. The boom is the air protesting.
why.try: A daylit fireball is the loud cousin.
why.tryLine: A daylit fireball is the loud cousin.

why.headline: Why impact craters are round even from a side hit?
why.summary: The explosion is outward from a point. Angle loses; blast wins.
why.try: A splash in milk does the same circle.
why.tryLine: A splash in milk does the same circle.

why.headline: Why the Moon has dark seas with no water?
why.summary: Old lava plains. Darker rock, not oceans. Sailors named them anyway.
why.try: Binoculars turn the names into places.
why.tryLine: Binoculars turn the names into places.

why.headline: Why we never see the Moon's far side from the sofa?
why.summary: It rotates in step with its orbit. We got the near face forever.
why.try: A spacecraft was required for the other cheek.
why.tryLine: A spacecraft was required for the other cheek.

why.headline: Why a new crescent has a ghostly full disk?
why.summary: Earth-light on the night part of the Moon. We are the lamp.
why.try: Look just after sunset. The ghost is us.
why.tryLine: Look just after sunset. The ghost is us.

why.headline: Why Venus outshines every star?
why.summary: Close, cloudy, and it reflects like a white pebble. A star would need to be rude to compete.
why.try: It will be west or east, never at midnight high.
why.tryLine: It will be west or east, never at midnight high.

why.headline: Why Mars looks rust-coloured?
why.summary: Iron oxide dust. The planet rusted.
why.try: A telescope turns the rust into a disk with hints.
why.tryLine: A telescope turns the rust into a disk with hints.

why.headline: Why Jupiter's moons are a tiny line of pearls?
why.summary: Galileo saw them first with a tube. They swap places night to night.
why.try: Binoculars are enough. A tripod helps.
why.tryLine: Binoculars are enough. A tripod helps.

why.headline: Why Saturn once looked like it had ears?
why.summary: Rings, seen poorly. Better glass turned ears into a hat.
why.try: The rings vanish edge-on some years. Patience.
why.tryLine: The rings vanish edge-on some years. Patience.

why.headline: Why Pluto got demoted?
why.summary: A crowd of similar icy worlds turned up. The word planet got stricter.
why.try: It is still there. The argument is the name.
why.tryLine: It is still there. The argument is the name.

why.headline: Why the solar system has a junk drawer out back?
why.summary: Leftover ice balls that never made a planet. Pluto is the celebrity in the drawer.
why.try: A long year out there.
why.tryLine: A long year out there.

why.headline: Why some comets fall from so far we cannot see the cloud?
why.summary: A theoretical shell of icy leftovers. Gravity pokes one now and then.
why.try: The comet is the visitor. The cloud is the rumour.
why.tryLine: The comet is the visitor. The cloud is the rumour.

why.headline: Why a comet tail points away from the Sun?
why.summary: Solar wind and light shove the dust and gas. The tail is a wind sock.
why.try: Two tails sometimes: dust and ion, slightly split.
why.tryLine: Two tails sometimes: dust and ion, slightly split.

why.headline: Why showers are named after constellations?
why.summary: The streaks point back to a patch of sky. We name the patch, not the rock.
why.try: Perseids in August are the friendly ones.
why.tryLine: Perseids in August are the friendly ones.

why.headline: Why meteors in a shower seem to come from one spot?
why.summary: Parallel paths look like they meet in the distance. Same trick as train tracks.
why.try: Lie down. Let the radiant be behind you sometimes.
why.tryLine: Lie down. Let the radiant be behind you sometimes.

why.headline: Why cities steal the Milky Way?
why.summary: Wasted light up and sideways. The skyglow is a blanket.
why.try: A park with shields on lamps gives stars back.
why.tryLine: A park with shields on lamps gives stars back.

why.headline: Why astronomers use red light?
why.summary: Red bothers night vision less. The eye keeps its dark adaptation.
why.try: A phone with a red screen is a modern lantern.
why.tryLine: A phone with a red screen is a modern lantern.

why.headline: Why looking beside a faint galaxy helps?
why.summary: The sweet spot for dim light is not the centre of the eye. Sneak up on it.
why.try: Do not stare. Glance and it pops.
why.tryLine: Do not stare. Glance and it pops.

why.headline: Why planets twinkle less than stars?
why.summary: A planet is a tiny disk, a star a pinpoint. Air cannot shove a disk as easily.
why.try: If it does not twinkle, check a chart. It might be Jupiter.
why.tryLine: If it does not twinkle, check a chart. It might be Jupiter.

why.headline: Why some nights the Moon looks boil-y in a telescope?
why.summary: Turbulent air. Astronomers call it seeing. The boil is weather, not the Moon melting.
why.try: A still 3am beats a shaky 8pm.
why.tryLine: A still 3am beats a shaky 8pm.

why.headline: Why telescope lenses fog?
why.summary: They cool below the dew point. The sky is a radiator.
why.try: A gentle heater ring is the grown-up fix.
why.tryLine: A gentle heater ring is the grown-up fix.

why.headline: Why binoculars say 8x42?
why.summary: 8 times closer, 42 millimetre windows. Bigger windows, brighter night.
why.try: 8x is holdable. 15x wants a wall.
why.tryLine: 8x is holdable. 15x wants a wall.

why.headline: Why the bright circle in the eyepiece should match your pupil?
why.summary: Too big and you waste light. Too small and it is like peeking a keyhole.
why.try: In dark, pupils grow. Daytime glass can be smaller.
why.tryLine: In dark, pupils grow. Daytime glass can be smaller.

why.headline: Why a huge telescope has a tiny one taped on?
why.summary: The small one sees a wide patch so you can aim the cannon.
why.try: Red-dot finders are the same idea with less neck pain.
why.tryLine: Red-dot finders are the same idea with less neck pain.

why.headline: Why some big scopes look like a cannon on a box?
why.summary: A simple up-down, left-right mount. Cheap, huge mirror, no computer required.
why.try: A push with a fingertip is the motor.
why.tryLine: A push with a fingertip is the motor.

why.headline: Why some mounts beep and slew by themselves?
why.summary: A computer plus motors plus a sky map. You aligned it; it does the hunt.
why.try: Garbage in, galaxy out the wrong hole.
why.tryLine: Garbage in, galaxy out the wrong hole.

why.headline: Why one axis of a mount is tilted?
why.summary: It matches Earth's tilt so one motor cancels the spin. Stars stop drifting.
why.try: The tilt should equal your latitude.
why.tryLine: The tilt should equal your latitude.

why.headline: Why that tilted axis wants Polaris?
why.summary: Near enough to the pole for a night of tracking. Not exactly on it. Close is a career.
why.try: A phone app now argues with the screws.
why.tryLine: A phone app now argues with the screws.

why.headline: Why a Newtonian can go blurry after a car ride?
why.summary: The mirrors knocked out of line. Stars become seagulls.
why.try: A cheshire or a laser is the chiropractor.
why.tryLine: A cheshire or a laser is the chiropractor.

why.headline: Why an extra tube makes planets bigger?
why.summary: It stretches the focal length. More stretch, more wobble too.
why.try: Double, do not quadruple, on a shaky night.
why.tryLine: Double, do not quadruple, on a shaky night.

why.headline: Why a Moon filter?
why.summary: The Moon is rude in a big scope. A dimmer switch saves the retina.
why.try: Clouds on the Moon are not weather. They are your eye recovering.
why.tryLine: Clouds on the Moon are not weather. They are your eye recovering.

why.headline: Why you never look at the Sun through glass you found?
why.summary: It can cook an eye silently. Only a proper front filter.
why.try: The cheap eyepiece 'sun filters' of old are villains.
why.tryLine: The cheap eyepiece 'sun filters' of old are villains.

why.headline: Why a card behind an eyepiece can show sunspots?
why.summary: The scope becomes a projector. Your eye stays out of the beam.
why.try: A grown-up aims. You watch the card.
why.tryLine: A grown-up aims. You watch the card.

why.headline: Why some years the Sun is spotty and some it is blank?
why.summary: An 11-year magnetic mood. Spots are cool knots in the mess.
why.try: A projection in a peak year is a dotted orange.
why.tryLine: A projection in a peak year is a dotted orange.

why.headline: Why the Sun blows a wind?
why.summary: Hot atmosphere escaping. Earth wears a magnetic coat against it.
why.try: Auroras are the coat sparkling.
why.tryLine: Auroras are the coat sparkling.

why.headline: Why a solar storm can bother power grids?
why.summary: A shove of magnetised gas. Long wires on Earth become accidental antennas.
why.try: Sat-nav hiccups are the polite version.
why.tryLine: Sat-nav hiccups are the polite version.

why.headline: Why astronauts care about two doughnut belts?
why.summary: Trapped particles. Linger and you collect a dose.
why.try: The ISS orbit ducks under the worst of them.
why.tryLine: The ISS orbit ducks under the worst of them.

why.headline: Why a 1957 beep changed school?
why.summary: First artificial satellite. The beep was a metal 'we are here'.
why.try: A classroom globe got more interesting overnight.
why.tryLine: A classroom globe got more interesting overnight.

why.headline: Why the flag on the Moon looks like it waves?
why.summary: A rod holds the top. They twisted it. No air, no wave.
why.try: The wrinkle is a frozen shove.
why.tryLine: The wrinkle is a frozen shove.

why.headline: Why Moon dust is nasty?
why.summary: No weather to round it. Tiny blades. It stuck to everything.
why.try: A vacuum cleaner on the Moon would have a hard life.
why.tryLine: A vacuum cleaner on the Moon would have a hard life.

why.headline: Why pouring tea would be rude in orbit?
why.summary: Liquids cling and blob. Gravity is the pourer we forget.
why.try: A bag and a straw is the teacup.
why.tryLine: A bag and a straw is the teacup.

why.headline: Why you cannot cry properly in space?
why.summary: Tears ball up on the eye. No down.
why.try: A towel is the gravity.
why.tryLine: A towel is the gravity.

why.headline: Why toilets in orbit are air systems?
why.summary: Suction replaces fall. A fan is the waterfall.
why.try: Miss and you have a floating problem.
why.tryLine: Miss and you have a floating problem.

why.headline: Why astronauts strap into sleeping bags on a wall?
why.summary: No down, so they pick a wall and become a picture.
why.try: An arm float in front of the face is the local ghost.
why.tryLine: An arm float in front of the face is the local ghost.

why.headline: Why the ISS has a bay-window blob?
why.summary: Seven panes for Earth-watching. Morale is a system.
why.try: The most expensive window seat.
why.tryLine: The most expensive window seat.

why.headline: Why a robot arm lives outside the station?
why.summary: To catch visiting ships and shuffle parts. A hand the size of a bus.

why.headline: Why some boosters cannot shut up once lit?

why.headline: Why people with screwdrivers visited Hubble?

why.summary: To change the spacing. Different spacings, different sharpness.

why.headline: Why 'where is everybody?' is a serious question?

why.headline: Why a star can reveal a planet we cannot see?

why.summary: Gentle heat. Chocolate and egg hate surprises.
why.try: A simmer, not a shout, in the pan below.
why.tryLine: A simmer, not a shout, in the pan below.

why.headline: Why a cheesecake sits in a water bath?
why.summary: Even, humid heat. The middle sets without a quake turning into a canyon.
why.try: Foil on the tin so the bath stays outside.
why.tryLine: Foil on the tin so the bath stays outside.

why.headline: Why that foil matters?
why.summary: A soggy cheesecake is a swimming lesson.
why.try: A slow oven without a bath can also work. Pick a religion.
why.tryLine: A slow oven without a bath can also work. Pick a religion.

why.headline: Why a cake tin has a latch?
why.summary: So a fragile cake can leave without a somersault.
why.try: The latch is not a suggestion. Latch it.
why.tryLine: The latch is not a suggestion. Latch it.

why.headline: Why a paper sling?
why.summary: A handle for the cake. Dignity on the way out.
why.try: Two strips, a cross, extra overhang.
why.tryLine: Two strips, a cross, extra overhang.

why.headline: Why that paper does not go see-through and sad?
why.summary: A treatment that shrugs at fat.
why.try: Baking parchment is the upgraded cousin.
why.tryLine: Baking parchment is the upgraded cousin.

why.headline: Why some trays wear a rubber sheet?
why.summary: Nothing sticks, almost. A thousand uses, one storage sulk.
why.try: A cut on it is forever. Knives are not invited.
why.tryLine: A cut on it is forever. Knives are not invited.

why.headline: Why cakes leave the tin for a wire?
why.summary: Air under stops a wet bottom. Steam can leave.
why.try: Five minutes in the tin first so it does not collapse into your hands.
why.tryLine: Five minutes in the tin first so it does not collapse into your hands.

why.headline: Why icing goes on twice?
why.summary: A thin dirty layer traps crumbs. The second layer is the clean shirt.
why.try: Fridge between coats. Patience is the third layer.
why.tryLine: Fridge between coats. Patience is the third layer.

why.headline: Why a triangle of plastic makes roses?
why.summary: Pressure plus a shaped hole. The rose is a wrist movement.
why.try: A jar in the bag keeps it open while you fill. Tiny wisdom.
why.tryLine: A jar in the bag keeps it open while you fill. Tiny wisdom.

why.headline: Why so many metal tips?
why.summary: Each hole is a different sentence: star, leaf, grass, blob.
why.try: A grass nozzle on mashed potato is how kids eat lawns.
why.tryLine: A grass nozzle on mashed potato is how kids eat lawns.

why.headline: Why a bendy blunt knife?
why.summary: To spread without cutting. A trowel for icing.
why.try: Warm water, wipe, spread. The shine comes from the wipe.
why.tryLine: Warm water, wipe, spread. The shine comes from the wipe.

why.headline: Why cake decorators spin the cake?
why.summary: So the hand stays still and the cake does the commute.
why.try: A plate on a tea-towel is a home version.
why.tryLine: A plate on a tea-towel is a home version.

why.headline: Why we saw the dome off?
why.summary: So towers do not become leaning towers.
why.try: A ruler and cocktail sticks are a poor person's laser.
why.tryLine: A ruler and cocktail sticks are a poor person's laser.

why.headline: Why bakers paint cakes with sugar water?
why.summary: Moist and a place for flavour. A dry sponge is a regret.
why.try: A brush, not a flood.
why.tryLine: A brush, not a flood.

why.headline: Why some cakes are dunked in three milks?
why.summary: They were built to drink. The dunk is the recipe.
why.try: A night in the fridge is the last ingredient.
why.tryLine: A night in the fridge is the last ingredient.

why.headline: Why those biscuits are dipped, not soaked?
why.summary: A quick bath. A long bath is mush.
why.try: Coffee, not a swimming lesson.
why.tryLine: Coffee, not a swimming lesson.

why.headline: Why a bowl of layers is a whole personality?
why.summary: Cake, fruit, jelly, custard, cream. A timeline you can eat.
why.try: The glass bowl is so the timeline shows.
why.tryLine: The glass bowl is so the timeline shows.

why.headline: Why a banana in a bag with an apple is a crime?
why.summary: They hurry each other into brown.
why.try: Separate fruit is peace.
why.tryLine: Separate fruit is peace.

why.headline: Why a kiwi wears a fuzzy coat?
why.summary: A thin skin plus hairs that shrug off pests. We eat the coat if we want.
why.try: A spoon trick skips the coat. Both are legal.
why.tryLine: A spoon trick skips the coat. Both are legal.

why.headline: Why a pomegranate is a room of rubies?
why.summary: Each pip is a seed in a juice jacket. A fruit that is a crowd.
why.try: A tap with a spoon is the polite eviction.
why.tryLine: A tap with a spoon is the polite eviction.

why.headline: Why a fig is a flower turned inside out?
why.summary: The sweet bit is a packed bloom. Some kinds need a tiny wasp. Most shop figs skipped that plot.
why.try: The crunch is seeds, not gravel.
why.tryLine: The crunch is seeds, not gravel.

why.headline: Why a date is a sugar bomb on a tree?
why.summary: A desert fruit dried on the stalk. Energy for a long walk.
why.try: A stone in the middle is the next tree.
why.tryLine: A stone in the middle is the next tree.

why.headline: Why a raw olive is a dare?
why.summary: Bitter chemicals. Brine or lye teaches it manners.
why.try: The jar is a finishing school.
why.tryLine: The jar is a finishing school.

why.headline: Why capers are flower buds in salt?
why.summary: Picked shut, then pickled. A flavour bomb that never got to bloom.
why.try: Rinse if they shout too loud.
why.tryLine: Rinse if they shout too loud.

wins.headline: The ozone hole is shrinking
wins.summary: Countries banned the chemicals that were eating the sky's sunscreen. Scientists now measure the hole getting smaller. A giant problem, slowly reversing.
wins.try: The move was a treaty plus better fridges. Teamwork at planet scale.
wins.tryLine: The move was a treaty plus better fridges. Teamwork at planet scale.

wins.headline: Humpback whales came back from the brink
wins.summary: Hunting nearly wiped them out. Bans and watchers gave them decades of quiet. Many populations have rebounded enough that boats now have to share the water.
wins.try: If you ever whale-watch, look for the tail fluke. Each one is unique.
wins.tryLine: If you ever whale-watch, look for the tail fluke. Each one is unique.

wins.headline: Kids' blood lead levels crashed
wins.summary: Lead in petrol and paint used to quietly hurt brains. Laws pulled it out. Average levels in many countries fell hard. Policy can be a superpower.
wins.try: Old houses can still have lead paint. That's a grown-up check, not a kid job.
wins.tryLine: Old houses can still have lead paint. That's a grown-up check, not a kid job.

wins.headline: Humans wiped one killer disease off Earth
wins.summary: Smallpox used to scar and kill millions. Vaccines plus a worldwide hunt ended it in 1980. It is the only human disease we have fully erased.
wins.try: That is what 'the plan worked' looks like at planet size.
wins.tryLine: That is what 'the plan worked' looks like at planet size.

wins.headline: Some rivers got otters back
wins.summary: Cleaner water and protection let otters return to rivers that were empty. If you see one, that's a report card for the whole valley.
wins.try: A local wildlife page will tell you if otters live near you.
wins.tryLine: A local wildlife page will tell you if otters live near you.

wins.headline: Solar got cheap enough to flood the grid
wins.summary: Panels used to be a rich-country toy. Prices crashed. Now whole countries add solar faster than coal. The physics did not change. The cost did.
wins.try: Spot three roofs with panels on your next walk.
wins.tryLine: Spot three roofs with panels on your next walk.

wins.headline: Kids ran a little free library street
wins.summary: A box on a lawn. Take a book, leave a book. Some streets now have three. No app, no fee, just neighbours trusting kids with stories.
wins.try: If you pass one, swap one book. That's the whole game.
wins.tryLine: If you pass one, swap one book. That's the whole game.

wins.headline: Some coral is being grown in nurseries
wins.summary: Divers farm hardy coral and glue it back onto damaged reef. Not a full fix. It is a start, and fish move back in.
wins.try: Reef-safe sunscreen exists. That's a tiny assist.
wins.tryLine: Reef-safe sunscreen exists. That's a tiny assist.

wins.headline: Cities that built bike lanes got more bikes
wins.summary: Paint and kerbs changed who dared to ride. Kids included. Safer paths, more riders, fewer cars on short trips. Design beats nagging.
wins.try: Count bike lanes on your school route. Zero is a clue.
wins.tryLine: Count bike lanes on your school route. Zero is a clue.

wins.headline: Bag charges slashed plastic at the till
wins.summary: A few pence changed habits faster than posters. Many countries saw single-use bags crash. Small price, huge pile of plastic not made.
wins.try: Keep one tote by the door. Future-you will grab it.
wins.tryLine: Keep one tote by the door. Future-you will grab it.

wins.headline: A teen built a cheaper hearing test
wins.summary: Julian Wilson and others have built simple phone-based hearing checks so more kids get spotted early. Not a hospital. A screen and a plan.
wins.try: If someone talks loud at you a lot, a hearing check is kindness, not teasing.
wins.tryLine: If someone talks loud at you a lot, a hearing check is kindness, not teasing.

wins.headline: Beavers got invited back on purpose
wins.summary: They build wetlands that soak floods and help fish. Some rivers that were ditches now hold water again. A rodent as infrastructure.
wins.try: Look up a beaver dam photo. That's a living dam.
wins.tryLine: Look up a beaver dam photo. That's a living dam.

wins.headline: Dark-sky towns switched the lights down
wins.summary: Warmer, downward lamps cut glare. Stars came back. Turtles and owls got a quieter night. You can still see the pavement.
wins.try: On a clear night, count stars in one window of sky.
wins.tryLine: On a clear night, count stars in one window of sky.

wins.headline: Kids redesigned their own playground
wins.summary: Some schools asked pupils to map the boring bits, then rebuild. More climbing, more shade, fewer 'don't'. Behaviour got better because the place got better.
wins.try: Sketch one change that would make your break better. That's a brief.
wins.tryLine: Sketch one change that would make your break better. That's a brief.

wins.headline: A seed in a jar is a tiny win farm
wins.summary: Wet kitchen paper, a bean, a window. In days you get a root. Proof you can grow something on purpose.
wins.try: Start one bean tonight. Name it something silly.
wins.tryLine: Start one bean tonight. Name it something silly.

wins.headline: A good apology is a win, not a loss
wins.summary: Name the thing, skip the excuse, ask how to fix it. People remember the repair more than the mess. That's how teams stay teams.
wins.try: The script: 'I did X. That was unhelpful. What would help now?'
wins.tryLine: The script: 'I did X. That was unhelpful. What would help now?'

harvest.headline: Ruby-forming mineral found by Mars rover hints at violent impacts
harvest.summary: So far, most of the minerals found on Mars tell a story of lava poured out by ancient volcanoes, followed by long stretches in which water trickled through and slowly reshaped the rock. However, some rocks scattered across the Martian surface seem to hint at a different geological history—carrying the same material that forms rubies and sapphires.

harvest.headline: Nuking an asteroid on short notice could save us
harvest.summary: Readers of a certain age will remember a golden era of asteroid films, capped by two with very different endings. "Deep Impact" drove home the devastating consequences of letting a large piece of rock hit our planet, whereas "Armageddon," though arguably the kitschier of the two films, was an uplifting story about technical ingenuity and sacrifice.

harvest.headline: Surprise! Wax seems key in turning honeybee larvae into queens
harvest.summary: Kids learn in grade school that honeybees “create” a new queen bee by feeding a larva royal jelly. A new study find that the young bee’s diet may be only part of what crowns her queen. The chemical makeup of a small “room” in the hive where she grows up also appears to play a key role.

harvest.headline: Watch Newsround - signed and subtitled
harvest.summary: A signed version of Newsround is available to watch every weekday for children who use British Sign Language.

harvest.headline: NASA Selects Companies to Provide Payload Processing Services
harvest.summary: Credit: NASA NASA has selected four companies to provide payload processing facilities under the Spacecraft Processing Operations Contract on‑ramp provision. The provision enables qualified providers to offer commercial payload processing services for agency missions launching from multiple locations where capabilities were not available at the time of the initial contract award. Contract awardees are: All Points Logistics LLC Blue Origin LLC Firefly Aerospace L3Harris Technologies Inc.

harvest.headline: Colorful Collage of Tarantula Nebula
harvest.summary: Like a collage made of layered sheets of colored cellophane, a vibrant new image layers observations of a famous star-forming nebula from NASA space telescopes. The resulting cosmic “craft” reveals new details about the star formation region known as 30 Doradus, or the Tarantula Nebula.

harvest.headline: Hubble & Gaia solve our galaxy's merger mystery
harvest.summary: Our home galaxy, the Milky Way, grew to its current size in part by consuming smaller galaxies. Now, new data from the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope show definitive evidence of a dwarf galaxy merging with the young Milky Way galaxy in the earliest phases of its evolution. This finding extends our knowledge of our galaxy’s history 1.8 billion years farther back in time than before.

harvest.headline: Otterly adorable! Thien and Rizzo start new life together
harvest.summary: Keepers are hoping the pair will breed to help boost otter numbers.

harvest.headline: Total solar eclipse 2026 (Official ESA broadcast)
harvest.summary: Video: 01:10:42 We broadcast live from the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre in Spain as a total solar eclipse crossed Europe on 12 August 2026. The path of totality swept across Greenland, Iceland, Spain and a small area of northeastern Portugal, while much of Europe experienced a partial eclipse. A total solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between Earth and the Sun, completely blocking the face of the Sun.

harvest.headline: In Pictures: The winner of World's Ugliest Dog contest is crowned
harvest.summary: Rescued pug wins the World's Ugliest Dog contest in California. The competition aims to remind people that adopting a dog can be just as rewarding as buying one and their unique features are celebrated.

harvest.headline: Scientists Say: Phenology
harvest.summary: Phenology (noun, “Fen-AW-luh-jee”) Phenology is a field of science. It studies the seasonal and environmental cues that trigger life-cycle changes in living things. Imagine a tree as winter turns to spring.

harvest.headline: Total Solar Eclipse in Sunflower Field
harvest.summary: This composite image shows the progression of a total solar eclipse over San Millán de los Caballeros, Spain on, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026.

harvest.headline: Marine Biologists Solved a Wildlife Mystery From the Walkway of the Golden Gate Bridge: How the Harbor Porpoise Mates
harvest.summary: The dolphin-like marine mammals returned to San Francisco Bay in 2008 after a decades-long absence from the area. Scientists took the rare opportunity to closely observe their behavior, and what they uncovered might help at-risk porpoise populations

harvest.headline: A look back at the 2026 total solar eclipse
harvest.summary: On 12 August 2026, Europe witnessed the first total solar eclipse in over two decades. Millions of people were awed by the Moon completely covering the Sun's bright disc, briefly turning day into night and revealing the Sun's outer atmosphere. Totality could be seen from Greenland, Iceland, Spain and Portugal, while most of the rest of Europe saw a partial eclipse.

harvest.headline: Perseids Meteor Shower
harvest.summary: The constellation Orion is framed by two Perseid meteors on Aug. 12, 2018, in Cedar Breaks National Monument, Utah.

harvest.headline: Explainer: What is ADHD?
harvest.summary: School was difficult for Makayla Caliendo when she was young. She remembers staring out the window while her classmates were paying attention in class. Some clothes, tags and socks were uncomfortable and left her unable to focus.

harvest.headline: Could Psilocybin Help Treat Anorexia? A Small Clinical Trial Suggests the Psychedelic May Make Patients More Open to Recovery
harvest.summary: The drug, paired with intensive psychological support, may loosen the rigid patterns of thought associated with the eating disorder, scientists say—but they caution that it is not a magic cure

harvest.headline: 'Like a Hole in the Universe': Artemis 2 Astronaut Victor Glover Reflects on Seeing a Total Solar Eclipse While Flying by the Moon
harvest.summary: The four astronauts who rounded Earth’s natural satellite in April got an extremely rare view of the dark lunar disk blocking out the sun. Researchers say the observations provide unique scientific value for understanding our star’s mysteries

harvest.summary: Do any shapes seem to jump out at you from this interstellar field of stars and dust? The jeweled expanse, filled with faint, starlight-reflecting clouds, drifts through the night in the royal constellation of Cepheus.
